lines.textEn: I still have questions. You there? (Knock on the door)

lines.textCh: 喂？有人吗？(敲门)
lines.textEn: Anyone there? Hello! (Knock on the door)

lines.textCh: 别紧张。甲板上已经没有其他敌人了，只有我们。
lines.textEn: Relax. There are no enemies left on the deck, just me.

lines.textCh: 总有其他路能进到舰桥里吧。
lines.textEn: There must be another way in.

lines.textCh: 离开
lines.textEn: Leave

lines.textCh: 我是不会开门的！快走开！
lines.textEn: I’m not opening! Go away!

lines.textCh: 外面现在已经安全了，出来吧。
lines.textEn: It’s safe now. Come out.

lines.textCh: 我才不信！要是你想着强行把门撬开，你绝对会后悔的！
lines.textEn: No! And if you try to break the door down, you’ll regret it!

lines.textCh: 你他妈到底是有什么毛病？
lines.textEn: What the hell is your problem?

lines.textCh: 我手里有非常危险的生物材料。要是任何人敢打破门冲进来，我就直接把这容器给打开！
lines.textEn: I have dangerous biomaterials in my possession. If anyone attempts to breach this door, I’ll open the container!

lines.textCh: 我把外头都清理干净了。船上到底发生什么了？
lines.textEn: The area is clear now. What happened on the ship?

lines.textCh: 你是瞎吗？！有人袭击了整艘船！
lines.textEn: Can’t you see?! The ship was attacked!

lines.textCh: 你他妈能不能冷静点！我已经把整层甲板都给清干净了！
lines.textEn: Calm the fuck down already! I cleared the whole deck!

lines.textCh: 我重复一遍：要是你敢破门而入的话，我就要被迫采取极端措施了！现在赶快给我滚！
lines.textEn: I repeat: if you attempt to breach the door, I will take extreme measures! Get the hell away from here!

lines.textCh: 你是打算在这里面蹲上多久，嗯？！
lines.textEn: And how long are you planning to sit in there, huh?!

lines.textCh: 想待多久就待上多久！在我看到船长之前，我是不会被你们骗出来的！
lines.textEn: As long as it takes! And until I see the captain, I’m not even coming near the door!

lines.textCh: 要是我拿他的录音在门口放，你恐怕也分辨不出来吧，你这个固执的傻瓜蛋！
lines.textEn: You wouldn’t even notice if I played you a recording of his voice, you moron!

lines.textCh: 我这可是有摄像头……傻瓜蛋！
lines.textEn: There’s a camera here… moron!

lines.textCh: 你觉得我会相信这种鬼话吗？
lines.textEn: You expect me to believe that?

lines.textCh: 我可不是和那群强盗一起上船的。要是你不愿意出来也行，至少告诉我你当时都看到了什么。
lines.textEn: I didn’t come here with the attackers. If you won’t come out, at least tell me what you saw.

lines.textCh: 我看到了什么？一场突袭！就在我们打破无线电静默之后，就有一群雇佣兵登上了船！
lines.textEn: What did I see? An assault! After we broke radio silence, mercenaries boarded the ship!

lines.textCh: 为什么 Boreas 号突然和外界联系了？你们明明已经在原地待了这么长时间都没挪窝。
lines.textEn: Why did the “Boreas” make contact? You’ve been sitting here for years.

lines.textCh: 因为有一些傻子不知道怎么遵守指令，这就是原因！
lines.textEn: Because a pair of idiots didn’t know how to follow orders, that’s why!

lines.textCh: 看样子你不是很在乎他们的死活啊。
lines.textEn: Their deaths don’t seem to bother you much.

lines.textCh: 为什么我要在乎那帮海员的死活？他们就和没长脑子一样，根本不明白船上装载的东西有多重要！
lines.textEn: Why should I care about laborers without brains? They had no understanding whatsoever of the importance of what’s being transported here!

lines.textCh: 所以到底是什么？
lines.textEn: And what exactly is that?

lines.textCh: 我没有透露这种机密信息的权限，直到看到船长之前，我不会多说一个字！
lines.textEn: I don’t have clearance to disclose such secrets. Without the captain, I’m not saying another word!

lines.textCh: 那行吧……所以我该上哪去找你那个船长？
lines.textEn: Okay then… So where do I find your captain?

lines.textCh: 袭击发生的时候他在舰桥上， 并且成功启动了船上的防御协议。你是没法轻易找到她的。
lines.textEn: During the attack he was on the bridge, and he managed to activate the defense protocol. You won’t reach him easily.

lines.textCh: 这样一来我得弄到通行权限才行。我到底该怎么去舰桥上？
lines.textEn: Then I need access. How do I get to the bridge?

lines.textCh: 这是机密！
lines.textEn: That information is classified!

lines.textCh: 要是我连舰桥都去不了，我他妈上哪去给你把那个该死的船长找来？！
lines.textEn: How the hell am I supposed to bring you the captain if I can’t even reach the bridge?!

lines.textCh: 啊，去他的保密条例。我直说吧：你得拿到他们发给海员的钥匙卡才能去舰桥那，那些密闭门光靠蛮力是没法强行打开的。
lines.textEn: Ah, to hell with it. You won’t get into the bridge without a sailor keycard, brute force won’t get those doors open.

lines.textCh: 我该上哪去弄到这些钥匙卡？
lines.textEn: And where do I get these keycards?

lines.textCh: 当时没人想到会启动防御协议，所以水手身上肯定没带着那些卡片。钥匙卡很可能还留在他们的个人舱室里，在上层甲板。
lines.textEn: The sailors didn’t carry them around because nobody expected the protocol to activate. They most likely left them in their cabins on the upper decks.

lines.textCh: 舰桥有一扇外门一直关不严，最近才修过。搞不好你能直接破开。
lines.textEn: One of the external bridge doors was repaired recently. You might be able to force it open.

lines.textCh: 那扇门就在这一层甲板上吗？
lines.textEn: Is that door somewhere on deck?

lines.textCh: 在轮机舱顶上。但要进入轮机舱，你得先从工程师身上搞到轮机舱钥匙卡才行。和水手不一样，船上的工程师一直随身带着钥匙卡。
lines.textEn: On top of the engine section. But to get there, you’ll need an engineer keycard. Unlike the sailors, the engineers always kept theirs on them.

lines.textCh: 明白了。
lines.textEn: Got it.

lines.textCh: 看来是我自讨没趣了…… (离开)
lines.textEn: Well guess I’ll go fuck myself then… (Leave)

lines.textCh: 你还在那吗？
lines.textEn: You still there?

lines.textCh: 那你倒是说说看我能上哪去？
lines.textEn: Where else would I go?

lines.textCh: 我需要你的帮助。我确实上到了舰桥，但往前走了一段，发现一扇有密码锁的门。并且电梯也没法用了。
lines.textEn: I need help. I made it to the bridge, but farther up I found a door with a keypad lock. And the elevators aren’t working.

lines.textCh: 所以确实没别的路子了……算了，我就帮你这一次。但你得保证你会把船长带到这来，还要确保他的安全！
lines.textEn: So there truly are no other options… Fine, I’ll help. But you’ll bring the captain here and guarantee his safety!

lines.textCh: 成交，所以密码是什么？
lines.textEn: Deal. So what’s the password?

lines.textCh: 密码由两部分组成。第一个和破冰船本身有关，第二个则是 TerraGroup 分部的区域代码。
lines.textEn: It consists of two parts. The first is connected to the icebreaker. The second is the regional code of a TerraGroup division.

lines.textCh: 哪一个分部？
lines.textEn: Which division?

lines.textCh: 当然是最近的那个！但是这部分代码是从岸上的分部直接发过来的。船上没有记录。
lines.textEn: Obviously the nearest one! But that code is transmitted from the mainland. There’s no such information aboard the ship.

lines.textCh: 那看来我得翻遍整个塔科夫去找这段该死的密码了……但你们总该知道上半部分吧？
lines.textEn: Guess I’ll have to search for it in the city myself. What’s the first part of the code?

lines.textCh: 等一等…
lines.textEn: One moment…

lines.textCh: 你还挺喜欢让别人等你的哈？
lines.textEn: Keeping me waiting, huh?

lines.textCh: 找到了。上半部分是：312。
lines.textEn: Found it. The code is: 312.

lines.textCh: 最好是把它记下来…
lines.textEn: Better write that down…

lines.textCh: 别他妈在这附近乱开枪！
lines.textEn: Stop shooting around here!

lines.textCh: 求你了，不要开枪！
lines.textEn: Please, cease fire!

lines.textCh: 啊！别开枪！
lines.textEn: Aah! Don’t shoot here!

lines.textCh: 别开枪！
lines.textEn: Don’t shoot!

lines.textCh: 快点滚开，别靠近！
lines.textEn: Get away from here!

lines.textCh: 这样真的安全吗？
lines.textEn: Is this actually safe?

lines.textCh: 好吧，我会去问问的，但没法向你保证。
lines.textEn: Alright. I’ll ask around. But no promises.

lines.textCh: 那我能得到什么好处？
lines.textEn: And what’s in it for me?

lines.textCh: 我进到舰桥里面了。
lines.textEn: I made it to the bridge.

lines.textCh: 那船长人呢？！都这种时候了你还在想着骗我？！
lines.textEn: Then where is the captain?! Are you trying to deceive me?!

lines.textCh: 冷静点！我没想过骗你，但你要找的船长早就死了。
lines.textEn: Calm down! I kept my word, but your captain is dead.

lines.textCh: 怎么证明你没在说谎？
lines.textEn: How can you prove that?

lines.textCh: 整个舰桥都被直升机火力给撕碎了。窗户是防弹的没错，但根本挡不住。船长身上带着一张黑色的钥匙卡，和别的船员都不一样，这就是我看到的情况。
lines.textEn: The whole bridge was riddled with machine gun fire from the helicopter. The windows were armored, but it wasn’t enough. The captain had a black keycard on him, unlike the rest of the crew.

lines.textCh: 我的天啊… 真该死…
lines.textEn: God damn it… Shit…

lines.textCh: 你还好吗？
lines.textEn: You alright in there?

lines.textCh: 一切还没有失控，没有！但那些样本……它们不能继续再留在船上了。
lines.textEn: Everything is under control! But the materials… They can’t stay here much longer.

lines.textCh: 你突然发什么疯？这些东西从塔科夫封锁以来么长时间了，不是一直留在船上，这也没出现过问题。
lines.textEn: What’s the problem, then? You managed to store them all this time, even after years in Tarkov.

lines.textCh: 那些雇佣兵发动袭击的时候，容器的完整性已经受损。必须马上把这些东西从船上撤离！
lines.textEn: During the assault, the integrity of the containers was compromised. They need to be evacuated from the ship immediately!

lines.textCh: 那就把门打开！我们可以坐直升机一起逃出这里。
lines.textEn: Then open the door! We can get out of here by helicopter.

lines.textCh: 不！太危险了。没错…没错，绝对不能坐直升机，直升机就是死！
lines.textEn: No! Far too dangerous. Yes, yes, absolutely no helicopters!

lines.textCh: 那你到底想让我干什么？
lines.textEn: Then what exactly do you want from me?

lines.textCh: 给我找一条下船的安全通道… 我负责会把东西准备好，去疏散。
lines.textEn: Find me safe transport… And I’ll prepare the materials.

lines.textCh: 所以到底是为什么不能坐直升机？
lines.textEn: What’s wrong with the helicopter evac?

lines.textCh: 什么，你难道想感染整个城市吗？！不，绝对不能从空中走，绝对不行……
lines.textEn: What, you want to infect the whole city?! No, nothing airborne, absolutely not…

lines.textCh: 那我能得到什么好处？
lines.textEn: And what’s in it for me?

lines.textCh: 我会把我的钥匙卡给你，通往我的实验室。里面有很多宝贵的设备，会有人愿意出高价的。
lines.textEn: I’ll hand over the keycard to my compartment. There’s a fortune in equipment here that people will pay dearly for.

lines.textCh: 行吧。但我没法保证一定能给你安排。
lines.textEn: Fair enough. But I’m not promising anything.

lines.textCh: 一切都在掌控之中！但我必须尽快离开这个地方。
lines.textEn: Everything is under control! But I need evacuation as soon as possible.

lines.textCh: 我可不会去碰你那些生化材料的，哥们。
lines.textEn: I’m not touching those biomaterials, dude.

lines.textCh: 我不会让你碰的！还有其他人能… 安排撤离吗？
lines.textEn: You won’t have to! Who else could… help arrange an evacuation?

lines.textCh: 好吧，我会想办法解决。
lines.textEn: Alright. I’ll handle it.

lines.textCh: 我会把我的钥匙卡给你，通往我的实验室。里面有很多宝贵的设备，会有人愿意出高价的。
lines.textEn: I’ll hand over the keycard to my compartment. There’s a fortune in equipment here that people will pay dearly for.

lines.textCh: 行吧。
lines.textEn: Fair enough.

lines.textCh: 也许你能用这架直升机把我带出塔科夫？
lines.textEn: So maybe you could fly me out of Tarkov on it too?

lines.textCh: 你这日子过得挺滋润啊！为了维持这种生活，是不是得花不少钱打点关系？
lines.textEn: You’ve got yourself set up pretty well! Had to grease a lot of palms to keep it?

lines.textCh: 我要去的地方 BTR 去不了。
lines.textEn: It won’t get me where I’m going.

lines.textCh: 哦？那个该死的 BTR 去不了？ 你他妈到底是打算上哪儿去？
lines.textEn: Oh yeah? That damn BTR can’t make it? Where the hell are you trying to get to?

lines.textCh: 有一艘船，就在塔科夫外海不远的地方，我得想办法登上去。
lines.textEn: There’s a ship sitting offshore near Tarkov. So I need something that can actually reach it.

lines.textCh: 所以你是上我这要船来了。 但问题是，我们这算是陆军。我甚至想不出谁能帮上忙。不过…… 也许还有法子。
lines.textEn: So you need a boat. Problem is, I’m more of a ground forces type. Don’t even have anyone to ask. Although... There might be another way.

lines.textCh: 是吗？
lines.textEn: Oh yeah?

lines.textCh: 我在基地里藏了一架直升机，你懂的，为了应对特殊情况。 但这事情你知我知，明白了吗？
lines.textEn: For special cases, I’ve got a bird tucked away at my base. But you better keep that to yourself, got it?

lines.textCh: 想想就知道，我不觉得整个塔科夫还有能飞的直升机。
lines.textEn: Didn’t think anything like that is still running in Tarkov.

lines.textCh: 动脑子可不是你的本职工作，对吧？ 只要和关键人物搞好关系，没有什么不可能的。
lines.textEn: Thinking’s not your job now, is it? Just have to be slick with the right people.

lines.textCh: 你的意思是，你成功说服了上级，让你在塔科夫留着一整架武装直升机？
lines.textEn: You’re saying you managed to talk your bosses into keeping a combat helicopter in Tarkov?

lines.textCh: 也许的确是这样，也许我根本不需要这么做！ 又或者，按照文件上的定义，它已经不再是军用直升机了…
lines.textEn: Maybe I did, maybe I didn’t! And maybe it’s not even a combat bird…

lines.textCh: 等等，那这么说，它还能飞吗？
lines.textEn: Hold on. Is it even operational?

lines.textCh: 你是不是忘了自己在和谁说话了，嗯？ 以你的军衔，恐怕还轮不到你指点上面是怎么做事的。
lines.textEn: You forget who you’re talking to, huh? You don’t have the rank to worry about how things get done up top.

lines.textCh: 你对我的背景一无所知，包括军衔。
lines.textEn: You don’t know anything about my background or my rank.

lines.textCh: 因为我他妈根本不在乎！你是在塔科夫，不是在什么狗屁新兵训练基地。 如果你还想我帮你的忙，就最好放尊敬些。
lines.textEn: Because I don’t give a damn! You’re in Tarkov, not on a training ground. So watch what you say if you want help.

lines.textCh: 行吧。但武装直升机可不是弹药箱这种小物件，你可没法像走私弹药一样随便找个角落就能藏起来。你到底是怎么做到的？
lines.textEn: Fair enough. Still, a combat vehicle isn’t some ammo box. You don’t just hide something like that in a corner. How’d you pull it off?

lines.textCh: 我可没说过那是军用直升机，而且我也不打算告诉你我是怎么搞到它的。
lines.textEn: I never said it was a combat bird. And I’m not telling you how I got it.

lines.textCh: 等等，那这么说，它还能飞吗？
lines.textEn: Hold on. Is it even operational?

lines.textCh: 你是不是觉得自己成个人物了，嗯？是不是，菜鸟？这玩意一靠近封锁线就会被打下来的，蠢货！
lines.textEn: You think pretty highly of yourself, huh, rookie? They’d shoot it down at the cordon, dumbass!

lines.textCh: 但在塔科夫封锁区里飞就没事？
lines.textEn: So they’re not gonna shoot it inside the Tarkov zone?

lines.textCh: 只要按照正确的航线飞，就没人会向它开火。
lines.textEn: If you fly it to proper spots, no one touches it.

lines.textCh: 那架直升机可是个货真价实的美人！你看到它就知道了。不过，如果能在起飞前给上上下下的部件再润滑一下就再好不过了。
lines.textEn: This beauty will outlive you! Still, it wouldn't hurt to grease a few things before takeoff.

lines.textCh: 所以我还得负责把它给修好了？
lines.textEn: So I’ve gotta fix it too?

lines.textCh: 等等，一开始来这低三下四地请人帮忙的好像不是我吧？ 这他妈搞不好可是封锁区里唯一一架还能动弹的飞机了，结果你还来劲了！
lines.textEn: Hold on a second, was that me coming to you with fucking requests? This might be the only working bird left in the city and you’re turning your nose up!

lines.textCh: 好吧，所以到底要我做什么？
lines.textEn: Fine. What needs to be done?

lines.textCh: 狗腿们会处理好的。但他们得跑一趟储备站，就是那个军事基地。 你得保证那里一切安全才行。
lines.textEn: My guys will handle it. But they’ll need to pay a visit to the Reserve military base. You make sure it’s safe there.

lines.textCh: 具体要针对哪些目标？
lines.textEn: Any specific targets?

lines.textCh: 不，你只要清理一下整个地方，确保我的机师到了之后没人向他们开火就行。 办完之后记得在通往 Priozersk 森林保护区的路上打一颗信号弹。到时候他们就从那儿进来。
lines.textEn: Nah. Just make sure nobody’s shooting at my techs when they get there. Once you’re done, fire a signal flare where the path meets the Priozersk forest. That’s where they’ll come in.

lines.textCh: 我不是来求你施舍的，我愿意接任务。
lines.textEn: Not asking for a handout. I can take on a difficult job.

lines.textCh: 我没让你免费帮忙，我会给钱的。
lines.textEn: Not for free. I can pay.

lines.textCh: 哦，是啊，当然了。我的价格是一百万……不，一万万卢布！
lines.textEn: Oh yeah, sure. My price is a million… no, a million millions roubles!

lines.textCh: 我还以为能和你正常做生意呢。
lines.textEn: I thought you were a businessman.

lines.textCh: 我不建议你想太多，因为你的脑瓜实在是不太灵光。你觉得光用钱就能弥补之前的那场闹剧？太荒唐了。不过我有其他需求，而且是立刻马上。
lines.textEn: I wouldn’t recommend you do too much thinking. Money won’t cover a screw-up like that. But I’ve got something I need, pronto.

lines.textCh: 所以，互帮互助？
lines.textEn: So, a favor for a favor?

lines.textCh: 没错，给我找几个军用滤波器来。然后我们就可以商量，怎么把你弄到你要去的地方。
lines.textEn: Yeah. Bring me a few military-grade power filters. Then I’ll get you where you need to go.

lines.textCh: 但你甚至都没问我要的是什么交通工具…
lines.textEn: But you didn’t even ask what kind of transport I need…

lines.textCh: 哼……你这家伙运气不错，非常不错。我确实需要点东西，立刻、马上。
lines.textEn: Hm… Lucky you. Very lucky. I do need something, pronto.

lines.textCh: 所以我们可以做笔交易咯？
lines.textEn: So we have a deal?

lines.textCh: 没错。给我找几个军用滤波器来，我会想办法安排交通工具的，送你上西天都可以。
lines.textEn: Yeah. Bring me a few military power filters, and I’ll sort out transport for you.

lines.textCh: 但你甚至都不知道我要的是什么交通工具…
lines.textEn: You don’t even know what kind of transport I’m looking for…

lines.textCh: 你爱去哪去哪！我的直升机能把你带到任何地方，只要不是塔科夫以外的地方都行。
lines.textEn: I don’t give a damn. My helicopter can get you anywhere, as long as it’s not out of Tarkov.

lines.textCh: 你搞到了一架直升飞机？！
lines.textEn: You have a helicopter?!

lines.textCh: 我这的好东西多得是。但在你带着我要的滤波器回来见我之前，你的那些请求在我这就是个屁。
lines.textEn: I’ve got a lotta things. But until you bring me those filters, I’m not even thinking about your request.

lines.textCh: 等等，这架飞机还能飞吗？
lines.textEn: Wait. Is it even operational?

lines.textCh: 我要去的地方 BTR 去不了。
lines.textEn: The BTR won’t get me where I need to go.

lines.textCh: 哦？这倒是新鲜，所以你到底要上哪儿去？
lines.textEn: Oh? And what kind of place is that?

lines.textCh: 塔科夫外海停着一艘船，我需要想办法到船上去。
lines.textEn: There’s a ship not far from Tarkov. I need to get on it.

lines.textCh: 嗯……我觉得还是有法子能安排的。你恐高吗？
lines.textEn: Hm… I think we can work something out. You afraid of heights?

lines.textCh: 等等……你弄到了一架直升机？！
lines.textEn: You’ve got a helicopter?!

lines.textCh: 没错，我是有一架。留着给特殊情况下用的，但如果你真的需要的话，我确实能帮上忙。
lines.textEn: I’ve got one, yes. I keep it for special situations, but if you really need it, I can help.

lines.textCh: 哈哈，所以事情真的是这样的吗？一架武装直升机在疏散中就这么“凑巧”留在了某个准尉的基地里？
lines.textEn: Just like that? A combat helicopter that just “happened” to stay on a warrant officer’s base during the evacuation?

lines.textCh: 呃，其实它不算是武装直升机…
lines.textEn: Well, it’s not exactly combat…

lines.textCh: 那到底是什么直升机？你是从哪搞来的？
lines.textEn: Then what is it? And where did you get it?

lines.textCh: 好吧，我会告诉你的。但要是有其他人问起来，可别到处说 Prapor 有一架直升机什么的，明白了吗？
lines.textEn: Alright, I’ll tell you. But if anyone asks, Prapor doesn’t have any helicopter, understood?

lines.textCh: 明白了。
lines.textEn: Understood.

lines.textCh: 我在 EMERCOM 有个朋友，你知道的，紧急情况部，当初我们刚入伍那会就经常偷偷一起溜出去… 之后他就在当地参加工作，负责搜救和灭火之类的——当然，前提是地方消防部门应付不过来的情况下。
lines.textEn: I’ve got a friend from EMERCOM, back during conscription we used to sneak out together… He worked in the region, search and rescue, putting out fires when fire watchers couldn’t handle it.

lines.textCh: 那你这个部里的朋友在“契约战争”期间都在干什么呢？
lines.textEn: And what were they doing during the Contract Wars?

lines.textCh: 你这是什么意思？EMERCOM 的人一直忙得团团转，直到封锁之前都在三班倒地干活，甚至冒着你们这些 PMC 的火力疏散平民。 反正最终是，他们有一架直升机严重受损，然后我私底下做了点安排，悄悄把它给“报废”掉了——总之，这架飞机名义上已经不再是政府财产了。
lines.textEn: What do you mean? Working non-stop. Three shifts until the blockade. Sometimes even under fire. Toward the end, one of their helicopters was badly damaged, and I arranged for it to be quietly “written off”.

lines.textCh: 难道这种程度的损失就没人过问吗？
lines.textEn: And no one questioned such a loss?

lines.textCh: 那时候城里的情况一团糟，根本管不过来，无论是就地维修还是疏散出去的风险都太高了，不如留在原地……实际上，大部分重装备就是这样被遗弃在塔科夫的。
lines.textEn: By that point, there was so much going on in Tarkov that repairing or evacuating it could’ve been more dangerous than leaving it there.

lines.textCh: 所以你把它完全修好了？
lines.textEn: So you fully restored it?

lines.textCh: 嗯，怎么说呢……如果能适当润滑一些部件的话，应该还是可以飞的。
lines.textEn: Well, how do I put it… If we grease a few spots, it should fly.

lines.textCh: 什么叫“应该”？
lines.textEn: It “should”?

lines.textCh: 别这么大惊小怪的，战士。我手下的机修师知道该怎么干活，他们之前已经让直升机顺利运转起来了。 但现在需要你自愿付出点劳动，好让飞机的工况恢复如新了。
lines.textEn: Relax warrior, my technicians know what they’re doing. They’ve already had this helicopter running before. But now it needs your voluntary participation.

lines.textCh: 需要我做些什么？
lines.textEn: What needs to be done?

lines.textCh: 储备站应该还留着一些特种油料，航空级别的，型号叫 AMG-10。 如果你能找来我需要的润滑油的话，我的人应该很快就能把直升机整备好。
lines.textEn: There should be some special oil left at the Reserve base, called AMG-10. If you bring it, my guys will get everything ready quickly.

lines.textCh: 我该从哪开始找？
lines.textEn: Where should I look for it?

lines.textCh: 去军营广场上那架米里直升机周围看看吧，如果那里没有的话，到火车站平台那边的仓库找找。哦，对了，搞不好军事学院的地下室里有，你应该知道的，标着黑主教棋子的那栋楼。
lines.textEn: Check near the MI bird at the barracks square. If it’s not there, search the cargo by the platforms or the basement under the academy building, Black Bishop.

lines.textCh: 明白了，我什么时候能收到你的消息？
lines.textEn: Got it. When should I expect to hear back from you?

lines.textCh: 疗养院旁边那个呢？
lines.textEn: What about the camp by the resort?

lines.textCh: 之前我从走私犯那儿弄过点零件，他们那边啥破烂都有，说不定也有能在水上漂的玩意儿。
lines.textEn: Picked up some parts from smugglers before, they’ve got all kinds of junk lying around. Might have something that floats too.

lines.textCh: 你能帮我跟他们牵个线吗？
lines.textEn: Can you put me in touch with them?

lines.textCh: 他们一般不跟你这种雇佣兵打交道。不过我可以帮你打听打听。
lines.textEn: They don’t usually deal with your kind. But I can ask around.

lines.textCh: 不是，就只准备“打听打听”吗？
lines.textEn: And you’d do that just like that?

lines.textCh: 别这样，我本来也要到他们那儿跑一趟的。不过你可以做点事，提高点成功率。
lines.textEn: Relax man, I’ll be heading that way anyway. But you could do something to improve your chances.

lines.textCh: 你需要什么？
lines.textEn: What do you need?

lines.textCh: 他们有几个藏匿点，最近老有外人过去晃悠。你把那些不请自来的“客人”清理掉，我会告诉那些走私者们是你在帮忙。
lines.textEn: They’ve got a couple of stashes where too many outsiders have been showing up lately. You clear out those “guests”, I’ll let the smugglers know it was you who helped.

lines.textCh: 行，那这些营地都在哪呢？
lines.textEn: Alright. Where are these camps?

lines.textCh: 一个在立交桥 Ultra 商场附近，另一个在海岸线码头北边，靠近疗养院那一带，用围栏围起来的那个。
lines.textEn: One’s near Ultra at the interchange. The other’s north of the port terminal, around where the health resort is.

lines.textCh: Ultra 商场附近的那个具体在哪？
lines.textEn: How do I find the one near Ultra?

lines.textCh: 从 Ultra 正门出来，过马路，再过一条铁轨就看到了。整个营地是用集装箱搭起来的，有大铁棚子、帐篷，还有一些临时搭的破屋子。那边有个红星标记，很显眼。
lines.textEn: Head out from Ultra, cross the road and the railway, you’ll run straight into it. Container camp, big canopy, tents, makeshift shacks. There’s a red star marking it, you won’t miss it.

lines.textCh: 海岸线不是有条路通往海关方向么？从疗养院东楼出发，往海关方向下坡，有一大片空地。过了那片地之后，你会看到几个棚屋和一些集装箱围起来的地方，那里就是了。
lines.textEn: Go down from the resort toward customs, there’s a big open field. Past that you’ll see a few hangars with shipping containers.

lines.textCh: 等你把事情搞定，我这边也差不多有消息了。
lines.textEn: By the time you’re done and back, I’ll have info for you.

lines.textCh: 那你认识的人里有谁能帮上忙吗？
lines.textEn: You know anyone who could help?

lines.textCh: 你是说这一切都怪我？
lines.textEn: You’re saying this is all on me?

lines.textCh: 你在说什么？
lines.textEn: What are you talking about?

lines.textCh: 别他妈装傻了，你个狗操的……当初我让你帮我摆脱 Skier，你倒好，全程站他那边！现在还有脸来找我帮忙？
lines.textEn: Don’t play dumb, fucko… Instead of helping me get out from under Skier, you backed him the whole way! And now you come asking me for help?

lines.textCh: 我当时没得选。
lines.textEn: I didn’t have a choice.

lines.textCh: 呵，现在说这种话就是放屁。因为你，我现在是麻烦缠身，几乎要撑不下去了。
lines.textEn: Oh yeah now that’s bullshit. Because of you I’m in such deep shit that I’m barely holding things together right now.

lines.textCh: 我可以想办法弥补。
lines.textEn: I can help fix that.

lines.textCh: 怎么补？你还能把时间倒回去重新选一次？
lines.textEn: How? You gonna roll back time and do things right?

lines.textCh: 我可以帮你弄到缺的东西，很快。
lines.textEn: I can get you whatever you’re missing, fast.

lines.textCh: 我现在缺的是“信任”……你懂吗？Skier 那个混蛋连弹药都不肯给我补满，你知道这对我的安全有多大威胁吗？
lines.textEn: What I’m missing right now is trust… I don’t even carry a full ammo load anymore, you get that?

lines.textCh: 那我想办法给你弄点弹药来。
lines.textEn: I’ll bring you ammo then.

lines.textCh: 这本来就是你该做的。别以为这样我们之间的恩怨就一笔勾销了。
lines.textEn: That’s the least you can do. And don’t think that fixes everything between us.

lines.textCh: 行，我去搞。
lines.textEn: Okay, I’ll handle it.

lines.textCh: 不然怪谁？我信过你，你却坑了我。
lines.textEn: Who else? I trusted you, and you burned me.

lines.textCh: 别什么都往我身上甩，我没时间听你扯淡。
lines.textEn: Don’t pin everything on me. I don’t have time for this.

lines.textCh: 那你那艘船就别想了。想让我考虑帮你，先把你给我惹的麻烦解决了。
lines.textEn: Then forget about your ship. If you want me to even think about helping, you fix the mess you got me into first.

lines.textCh: 好吧……你要什么？
lines.textEn: Alright… What do you need?

lines.textCh: 因为你，我现在出门跑车的时候连同轴机枪的备弹都找不齐了。给我带点子弹来。还有，别指望我马上就能信你。
lines.textEn: Because of you I don’t even have enough ammo for every run. Bring me rounds. And don’t expect trust after that.

lines.textCh: 嗯，说不定你认识其他人能载我一程？
lines.textEn: Well, maybe you know anyone who could help?

lines.textCh: 其实……还真有。那些走私者。他们手里有不少旧装备，说不定有船。
lines.textEn: Actually… yeah. The smugglers. They’ve got old gear lying around, they might have a boat.

lines.textCh: 我怎么联系他们？
lines.textEn: How do I reach them?

lines.textCh: 你自己去的话，他们连话都不会跟你说。不过我可以帮你问。
lines.textEn: If you go on your own, they won’t even talk to you, that’s for sure. But I can ask for you.

lines.textCh: 太好了。你需要我做什么？付钱？还是帮他们做点事？
lines.textEn: Perfect. What do you need from me? Payment? Do some job for them?

lines.textCh: 嗨呀，咱俩谁和谁啊！你帮我摆脱 Skier 那事我还能忘了？要不是你，我现在还在给他卖命呢！
lines.textEn: Oh come on, friend! You think I forgot how you got me out from under Skier? I’d still be slaving for him without you!

lines.textCh: 不过话说回来，在塔科夫没人愿意白干活，哪怕是帮忙。
lines.textEn: Still, nobody does anything for free in Tarkov.

lines.textCh: 这不算白帮。你当初帮了我大忙，现在只不过是轮到我帮你罢了。
lines.textEn: This isn’t for free. You helped me big time back then, and now I help you.

lines.textCh: 行吧……那我什么时候能有消息？
lines.textEn: Alright… When can I expect news from you?

lines.textCh: 我本来就打算一会去见一趟这些走私的。下次见面的时候，我就能给你答复。怎么样？
lines.textEn: I was planning on heading over there right now actually, so next time we meet, I’ll have an answer. Sound good?

lines.textCh: 听起来不错。
lines.textEn: Sounds good.

lines.textCh: 退出
lines.textEn: Exit

lines.textCh: 退出
lines.textEn: Exit

lines.textCh: 我收到了你的信号，快回话！
lines.textEn: I'm receiving your signal. Come in!

lines.textCh: （扬声器只发出机械噪声与干扰）
lines.textEn: (The speaker emits only mechanical sounds and interference)

lines.textCh: 你可真是帮了我一个大忙，要不是你及时把东西送到了，我这会儿恐怕还在使劲浑身解数和客户解释呢……
lines.textEn: Thanks for the help. If it weren't for you, I'd still be trying to patch things up with the client...

lines.textCh: 我是为了 Prapor 的事来的，我找到那个箱子了，虽说本来应该是他的人带到你这来。
lines.textEn: I'm here on Prapor's behalf. I found the case his men were supposed to deliver to you.

lines.textCh: 出门的时候当心点。
lines.textEn: Watch yourself on the way out.

lines.textCh: 这些可都是稀罕货。
lines.textEn: Those are quite rare.

lines.textCh: 办完了，这是我找到的所有材料，都是关于那个裁判的。
lines.textEn: Done, here’s everything I found on Ref.

lines.textCh: 好了，现在把报酬给我，我就自己走了。
lines.textEn: Okay, now give me my reward, and I'll be on my way.

lines.textCh: 很好。
lines.textEn: Good.

lines.textCh: 轻拿轻放。
lines.textEn: Be careful with it.

lines.textCh: 这单就这样吧，你很快就能拿到所有的数据了。
lines.textEn: Consider it done. Soon you'll have all the data.

lines.textCh: 很好。
lines.textEn: Good.

lines.textCh: 很好。
lines.textEn: Good.

lines.textCh: 返回
lines.textEn: Back

lines.textCh: 你应该明白独门消息自有其重大价值。如果你还想深挖那个裁判的底细，我可以帮你。
lines.textEn: You know the value of unique intel. If you want to know more about Ref, I can help with that.

lines.textCh: 明白。
lines.textEn: Got it.

lines.textCh: 很高兴你能明白，和谁做朋友更有利。
lines.textEn: I'm glad you understand who it's more advantageous to be friends with.

lines.textCh: 提醒你一下——我这里概不退款。
lines.textEn: No refunds, just so you know.

lines.textCh: 我听说你卷进了 Fence 和竞技场裁判之间的风波。也是，在招惹到这种人物之后，这里算是你唯一能来的地方了。你想报复一下那个裁判？嗯……这倒是可能会对我有利。去给我找点他的脏材料来，我会想办法利用好的。
lines.textEn: I heard you got involved in this affair with Fence and Ref. So of course you decided to come to me. You want to mess with Ref? Hmm, that would be beneficial to me. Bring me the dirt on him, and I'll find a way to use it.

lines.textCh: 我给黑色军团小队打了掩护，现在该告诉我这些家伙的身份，以及他们到底是在给谁干活了吧？
lines.textEn: I covered Black Division. Now are you gonna tell me who they are and who they're working for?

lines.textCh: 很好。
lines.textEn: Good.

lines.textCh: 行……但在这之后，我希望把一切查个水落石出，为了找出真相，我必须得到相应的情报。
lines.textEn: Fine... But afterward, I want to get to the bottom of what's going on, and for that I need info.

lines.textCh: 返回
lines.textEn: Back

lines.textCh: 最近塔科夫新出现了一群超级士兵，叫黑色军团之类的……你听说过这帮家伙的事情吗？
lines.textEn: Have you heard anything about that supersoldier unit that showed up in Tarkov? Black Division or something like that.

lines.textCh: 明白了。
lines.textEn: Understood.

lines.textCh:
你是真的缺乏理解能力，还是单纯不愿意接受现实？从一开始，USEC 就不过是 TerraGroup 手里趁手的工具、一枚好用的棋子而已。和任何工具一样，一旦实现了预定的目的，工具本身也就失去了价值。但和 USEC 不一样的是，黑色军团直接听命于那些左右世界局势的大人物——你应该清楚，这里说的并不是那些 TerraGroup 高管。

眼下集团在塔科夫最需要的不是保卫设施免受外界窥探的安保工具，而是远胜那些外来雇佣兵的精密仪器，用来定点清除所有不该遗留在城市里的资产。我实在不建议你干涉这场复杂的手术，免得自己也成为这座城市不受欢迎的那部分。
lines.textEn:
Do you really still not understand, or do you simply refuse to believe what you're seeing? USEC were a tool for TerraGroup from the very beginning. And like any tool, they lost their value once they had served their purpose. But unlike them, Black Division answer directly to those who shape the course of events in the world. And I'm not talking about TerraGroup's managers.

The corporation's facilities in Tarkov no longer need protection. The city requires a more precise instrument to surgically remove everything that has no place here. And I wouldn't advise you to interfere with the operation.

lines.textCh:
当然。不过和你们这些雇佣兵不一样的是，军团小队不仅是当下局势的塑造者，在未来的世界中还将继续扮演重要角色。

但我不会透露任何超出必要的信息。你已经和军团小队交过手了，显然，你打算靠自己或多或少地造成一些影响。但光是靠蛮力硬干什么也改变不了，只会把自己变成军团的下一个目标。

我建议你另作打算：先用实际行动弥补自己犯下的错误，说不定我会改变主意，透露一些你想要的情报。

首先，我们需要清理出一条路线。从海岸线出发，穿过储备基地，直抵森林，消灭中途遭遇的一切威胁。如果中途遇到了黑色军团成员，绝对不允许和他们交战，这是任务的一部分。
lines.textEn:
Of course. They aren't ordinary mercenaries. They play an important role in what's happening now and what will happen later.

But I'm not going to tell you more than you need to know. You've already crossed paths with them. Obviously, you want to influence something. But you won't change anything this way. You'll only become another one of their targets.

I propose a different arrangement. Correct your mistakes with your own hands, and perhaps I'll share the information you're looking for.

First, we need to clear one route. Follow the route from the coast to the woods through the military base and eliminate any potential threats along the way. But if you see Black Division, do not engage them under any circumstances.

lines.textCh: 我理解的情况是，黑色军团更像是一支清场小队，只不过行动规模覆盖整座城市而已。但很显然，他们正在集团的秘密设施里搜寻某些东西。
lines.textEn: As I understand it, Black Division is basically a cleanup crew, just on the scale of an entire city. But they're clearly looking for something at these facilities.

lines.textCh:
你拼尽全力想要看清事情的全貌，却忘了自己不过是其他势力手中的另一件工具而已。如果你的能力和好奇心相称的话，就必须跳出眼下的处境，抛开你所熟悉的冲突双方。

你真的下定决心要查明事情的真相了吗？那就仔细听好接下来的任务，必须严格按照我的指示去做，不能出现任何纰漏。

你需要从 14 号集装箱里回收一个箱子，把货物送到市区，最后发信号通知附近的黑色军团单位。

等你办完这件事之后再来见我。
lines.textEn:
You want to see the whole picture, but you forget that you're still just a tool. To learn more, you'll have to rise above the situation and forget about the sides of the conflict you're familiar with.

Are you sure you're ready to do that? Then listen to your next task. You need to follow the instructions exactly.

You need to take a case from Container 14, deliver it to the downtown, and signal the Black Division unit.

When you're done, come back to me.

lines.textCh: 如果我没有准备好就不会站在这了。
lines.textEn: I wouldn't be standing here if I wasn't ready to act.

lines.textCh: 我按照你说的把任务完成了。现在该轮到你告诉我箱子里是什么了吧，为了这个玩意我差点被人打得屁股开花！
lines.textEn: I did the job exactly as you instructed. Now tell me what I busted my ass for. What's in the case?

lines.textCh:
要是我事先就告诉你里面装了什么，你就不会接下这份差事了。不过别担心，我让你送的并不是什么病毒，也不是什么放射性的玩意。

不过你猜对了一件事：清理集团设施只是黑色军团职责的一部分，整个塔科夫还散落着大量珍贵的技术样本，而 TerraGroup 的竞争对手们至少得再花上十年才能把这些东西搞到手。至于这些样本是什么，以及都有什么作用，我是不会告诉你的。

有些东西的价值远在整座城市之上，甚至把塔科夫所有居民也计算在内，天平的指向也不会改变分毫。在这一过程中人们也许会死去，但无名者的赐福必须延续到新世界。等到黑色军团在塔科夫的行动结束后，就再也不会有任何事情能阻止行动实施了。
lines.textEn:
If I had told you what was inside, you wouldn't have agreed to this job. But don't worry, there's neither a virus nor radiation inside.

You were right about one thing. Black Division has assignments beyond clearing facilities. There are still samples in Tarkov that TerraGroup's closest competitors would need at least ten years to obtain. I won't tell you what they are or what they do.

Some things are worth more than the entire city and everyone living in it. People may die, but the gifts must survive into the new world. After Black Division's operation in Tarkov, there will be nothing left to stand in the way of the plan.

lines.textCh: 关于所谓的“赐福”，以及你提到的这个计划，我还想了解更多情况。这些神神叨叨的东西到底是怎么和黑色军团扯上联系的？
lines.textEn: I want to learn more about these gifts and this plan you mentioned. How does all this mysticism tie into the Black Division?

lines.textCh:
最好和见证者们去讨论这个，毕竟他们为了能见到无名者许诺的新世界可是不惜一切。

在新世界的法则下，绝大多数人将永无出头之日。但即便是最微不足道的行动和变化，也将在天翻地覆之后成为新世界里人类唯一所能仰仗的的基础。

仅仅身处塔科夫并不意味着就能参悟眼下的局势——尽管你早已是世界演变进程的一份子了。就算是肩负特殊使命的黑色军团也注定无法在那个世界重生。

他们会负责铺就道路，只有少数获选之人能有幸走上那条荣耀之路。如果你执意抗拒必将到来的命运，那么黑色军团也会对你展开猎杀。认清现实，然后接受它，这才是最明智的选择。

见证者汇报说，有一群不知天高地厚的 PMC 在夜间肆意干扰黑色军团干员们的行动。你必须出手制止这场闹剧，把猎物的狗牌带到仪式现场，作为最鲜活的证明。
lines.textEn:
It's better to discuss that with the Witnesses. They're willing to do anything to see the new world.

Most will never rise to prominence under the new rules. But even the smallest actions and events will become the foundation humanity will rely upon after the transition.

You probably won't understand the essence of the process you've already become a part of simply by being in Tarkov. Black Division has a special role to play, but even they aren't destined for rebirth.

They'll pave the way, a path that only a select few will be permitted to walk. If you resist the inevitable, Black Division will come for you as well. It would be wiser to accept reality.

The Witnesses report that a PMC group is interfering with Black Division's night-time operations. Put an end to it, and bring the dogtags of those you kill to the ritual sites as proof.

lines.textCh: 我可不打算加入你们那个地下教会。但如果能换来有关黑色军团指挥官，以及这家伙过往经历的情报，我愿意接下这个任务。
lines.textEn: I'm not joining any cults. But in exchange for information about the Black Division commander and his past, I'm willing to take this job.

lines.textCh: 我干掉了那些士兵，把狗牌留在了画有符号的仪式圈里。现在你该透露点 Wedge 的事情了，这家伙难道也是个邪教徒之类的？
lines.textEn: I took out those soldiers and left the dogtags in the circles with the symbols. Now I want the info on Wedge. Is he some kind of cultist too?

lines.textCh:
你总是试图把事情过度简单化，所谓的“邪教徒”与“正常人”之间并没有泾渭分明的红线。虽然我从未亲自和托马斯打过交道，但我能理解他是如何看待这个世界的。在 SAS 的多年服役经历显然起到了作用，加上那起最终导致他退出现役的事件……这家伙无论干出什么来我都不会觉得惊讶了。

在黑色军团单位里，他负责带队清理集团设施，以及消灭指定目标，恐怕这家伙无论到什么地方都找不到第二份这么适合他的工作了。Wedge 已经变成了一件完美的工具，用于执行特定任务无往而不利，但除此以外几乎毫无用处——与其说他是后来转变成这样的，不如说这家伙主动把自己异化成了一件工具。

当然，Wedge 并不相信世界的重生，以及随后必将到来的新秩序。但历史洪流就是这样，无论那些被卷入其中的人信仰如何，它都会裹挟着整个世界向前，不去理会任何异议。
lines.textEn:
You're trying to oversimplify the situation. I've never met Thomas personally, but I understand how he sees the world. Years of service in the SAS have done their work, and after the incident that got him removed from active duty... Nothing surprises me.

In Black Division, he works on operations to clear facilities and eliminate targets, and he likely wouldn't find a better use for himself anywhere else. Wedge became, or rather made himself into, a tool perfectly suited for specific tasks, but no longer useful for anything else.

Of course, he doesn't believe in rebirth or the new order that will come afterward. But history has never depended on the faith or opinions of the people caught in its millstones.

lines.textCh: 所以你在灯塔也有业务了？没想到能在这听见你的引擎声。
lines.textEn: So you're working around the Lighthouse area now, too? Didn't expect to hear your engine out there.

lines.textCh: 你的祝贺我就先收下了，呵呵！琢磨停靠站点的位置以及和本地的地头蛇安排几项“协议”是花了不少功夫，但现在一切都顺利起来了。顺便一提，关于停靠站点的事情，我想问问你的专业建议。有兴趣吗？
lines.textEn: Accepting your congratulations! Took some work to organize the stops and handle a few "arrangements", but everything's running smoothly now. By the way, you could still help me out with your professional opinion on the stops. Interested?

lines.textCh: 具体是个什么情况？
lines.textEn: What about them?

lines.textCh: 总的来说，我肯定是挑最安全的地方停车，但还是有几个地方我不太有把握，如果你能到现场去看看，然后回来把你的看法告诉我，那就再好不过了。
lines.textEn: Overall, I picked some pretty secure spots for them, but there are still a couple I'm not completely sure about. If you could check them out and tell me what you think afterward, that'd be great.

lines.textCh: 我该上哪去打探情况？
lines.textEn: Where should I look?

lines.textCh: 污水处理厂里的那个站点我最不放心，就是两间厂房中间的那个地方。之前那儿根本没法开车通过……接下来去村口的十字路口以及主路上的 UN 检查站看一眼。这两个地方都在开阔地，至少你应该知道在那儿下车会从哪个方向挨打，我好早些警告他们。
lines.textEn: The stop I'm least confident about is the one at the water treatment plant, between the two buildings. It used to be completely inaccessible by vehicle... Also take a look at the stops at the crossroads in the village and at the UN checkpoint on the main road. They're both out in the open, so maybe you can at least tell me where my customers should expect to get hit from.

lines.textCh: 听上去是个好事，让我坐车的时候也能安全些。
lines.textEn: It's a good cause, and it'll make things safer for me, too.

lines.textCh: 我把灯塔周边那些站点位置都检查过一遍了。
lines.textEn: I checked out the new stops around the Lighthouse area.

lines.textCh: 嗯？所以你的看法是？
lines.textEn: Well? What do you think?

lines.textCh: 十字路口最让人提心吊胆，整个地方几乎是四面漏风。最糟的是马路对面就有窗口对着，如果安排一场埋伏几乎无路可逃。如果真的有人打算在那儿下车，就得做好准备连滚带爬跑到那堆油桶和混凝土块后面才行。
lines.textEn: The crossroads is the most pucker factor spot. You can get hit from pretty much anywhere. The worst part is the windows of the house across the road, perfect spot for an ambush. Basically, if you're getting out there, you need to make a run for the barrel and the concrete barriers right away.

lines.textCh: 听起来实在是太操蛋了，不过我会和客户讲清楚的。那污水厂里的那个停车点，你觉得怎么样？
lines.textEn: That's pretty damn bad, but I'll pass it on to my customers. What do you think about the stop at the water treatment plant?

lines.textCh: 污水厂里的那块地周围倒是不缺掩体，但还是得下车就直奔藏身的地方才行。周围厂房屋顶和楼内都有不少地方能藏人。要是没买火力掩护就在那下车等于自投罗网。
lines.textEn: There's plenty of cover nearby, but you have to run to cover straight away. They can hit you from the roof or from inside the buildings themselves. Without your fire cover, getting out here could still be dangerous.

lines.textCh: 那主路上的停车点呢？你也看过的，靠近 UN 检查站的那个。
lines.textEn: And what about the main road? You know, the one with the UN checkpoint.

lines.textCh: 检查站永远是最显眼的地方，塔科夫也不例外。无论进出的道路都暴露在周边的火力之下，就算悬崖上没有蹲着狙击手，豪宅里的狗恐怕也忍不住往下面放两枪。所以如果哪个乘客打算在这下车，最好还是让他们小心点外边高处。
lines.textEn: A checkpoint's a checkpoint, even in Tarkov. The approaches are pretty exposed though, with shots most likely coming from the cliffs or the chalet side. So tell your customers to keep their eyes open while they're making their way to the stop.

lines.textCh: 明白了。谢谢你带来的情报，太重要了！虽然我自己没法改变下车点周围的情况，但至少我能给新来的菜鸟们提个醒。
lines.textEn: Got it. Thanks for the intel, this stuff matters! I can't fix the problems myself, but at least I'll pass your advice on to the younger guys.

lines.textCh: 如何，新路线跑起来怎么样？
lines.textEn: So, how's the new route treating you?

lines.textCh: 我该怎么说呢……眼下生意挺不错，但周围的 Scav 也变得越来越肆无忌惮了，根本不打算让我在这好好跑车。这帮土匪已经好几次试图在停车点埋伏我的乘客，甚至还把站点周围的东西都抢劫一空！
lines.textEn: How do I put it... Demand's good right now, but the Scavs are getting way too fucking bold. They won't let me work in peace. They try to ambush my passengers at the stops, and they're even looting the stops themselves!

lines.textCh: 难道你就不打算做点什么制止他们吗？
lines.textEn: And you're not gonna do anything about it?

lines.textCh: 他们专挑我不在的时候才来胡混！说不定你能帮我一把？我们需要杀鸡儆猴，把那些混混都给吓走，或者最好把这当成一项声明，告诉土匪们 BTR 要在海边长时间驻扎下去，他们再不乐意也没有办法！但我没法成天待在灯塔，毕竟还有 Priozersk 自然保护区和市区的生意要做。
lines.textEn: They only come around when I'm not there! Maybe you could help me out? We need to scare them off, or better yet, make it clear that the BTR is here on this stretch of coast for the long haul. I can't stay here all the time myself. I've got business in Priozersk and in the city, too.

lines.textCh: 那你有什么好法子吗？
lines.textEn: You got any solution to the problem?

lines.textCh: 你懂的，你可以制造点动静，让他们以为我还在灯塔，随时准备用机枪把他们送上天！用和车上同轴机枪一个口径的武器去放两枪，好好地敲打敲打他们——反正死鬼又没法告诉其他人开枪的不是 BTR 而是雇佣兵。这样他们应该就能接受我们定下的新规矩了。
lines.textEn: You know, you could make it look like I'm still around! Just use the same caliber my coax gun does. Once you scare the shit out of them, they'll probably get used to how things work around here now.

lines.textCh: 好，我会帮你的。
lines.textEn: Alright, I'll help you out.

lines.textCh: 我把 Scav 都吓跑了，应该达到了你想要的效果。
lines.textEn: I scared off the Scavs. I think I managed to create the effect you wanted.

lines.textCh: 嚯嚯，你可真是帮了我一个大忙，老兄！你的分身术演得不赖，连乘客都在问我是从哪搞来第二辆 BTR 的了……
lines.textEn: Well shit, you saved my ass, dude! My passengers are already asking where I got a second BTR from, since I'm somehow in two places at once...

lines.textCh: 来，拿着。我在自个的车库里找到的。这玩意当时就躺在地下室里，好不容易才拖出来的。
lines.textEn: Here, take this. I found it recently at my old depot base. Pulled it out of the basement there.

lines.textCh: 出岛的时候当心点。
lines.textEn: Keep your eyes open on your way out.

lines.textCh: 这些可都是稀罕货。
lines.textEn: Those are quite rare.

lines.textCh: 你说的我都照办了。
lines.textEn: I did everything you asked.

lines.textCh: 很好。
lines.textEn: Good.

lines.textCh: 轻拿轻放。
lines.textEn: Be careful with it.

lines.textCh: 好吧，我来搞定。
lines.textEn: Fine, I'll take care of it.

lines.textCh: 返回
lines.textEn: Back

lines.textCh: 看来那些走私犯给游荡者施加了不小的压力，把他们一路逼退到了度假村一带。你之前不是还想让他们继续守在污水处理厂那儿吗？
lines.textEn: Looks like the smugglers put some serious pressure on the Rogues and drove them back to the chalets. Weren't you interested in keeping them at the water treatment plant?

lines.textCh: 明白了。
lines.textEn: Understood.

lines.textCh: 你做的很好，看来整个过程没出什么意外。要是没有你的介入，游荡者恐怕连头几个星期都撑不过去，更别提站稳脚跟了。
lines.textEn: It's good that you managed to avoid any surprises. Without your involvement, the Rogues would've had a much harder time surviving those first few weeks.

lines.textCh: 我这里概不退款。
lines.textEn: I do not accept refunds.

lines.textCh:
你看起来不能理解我真正关心的是什么，撤退到度假村一带恐怕是他们唯一合理的选择了。很高兴看到地盘上的各方势力逐渐形成了新的平衡。

但我知道有些人想要彻底消灭游荡者，好让其中一个阵营从冲突中彻底退场。绝不能允许这种情况发生。所以，如果你有兴趣巩固自己在灯塔这边的地位，也许你可以参与到这场自卫行动中来。

你不需要跑到度假村区域以身试险——游荡者并不会因为你出手帮忙就客气多少。但如果你能在灯塔地带消灭几个不长眼的 PMC，我倒是愿意给些报酬。记住，不要试图和我作对。
lines.textEn:
You are unlikely to understand what it is I'm truly interested in. Their retreat to the chalets was the only correct move given the situation they found themselves in. And I'm quite satisfied with the new balance of power on my territory.

But I know some people want to destroy the Rogues completely, removing one of the factions from the conflict. That cannot be allowed. So, if you're interested in strengthening your position at the lighthouse, you may take part in their defense.

You don't need to enter the chalets themselves. The Rogues will shoot at you as well. But I'm willing to pay for eliminating PMC operatives in this part of the coast. Just don't work against me.

lines.textCh: 我自己也想和 Lightkeeper 合作，但他甚至不肯直接联系我。 他最多找我买些设备，就算是这样还要通过中间人。
lines.textEn: I'd be glad to work with Lightkeeper myself. But he doesn't even contact me directly. At most, he buys equipment from me. And even that's done through intermediaries.

lines.textCh: 所以你也没法和他联系上吗？
lines.textEn: So you don't have any way of contacting him yourself?

lines.textCh: 他选择合作对象的标准相当挑剔。 如果在这方面有任何进展，我会告诉你的，但你也必须明白一些东西。
lines.textEn: He's extremely selective about who he works with. I'll let you know if I make any progress on that front, but there's something you need to understand, too.

lines.textCh: 那是什么意思？
lines.textEn: What's that?

lines.textCh: 如果没能在塔科夫闯出名声来的话，Lightkeeper 根本不会考虑亲自和你会面的。 你还没有建立起足够的信任，没有资格踏入那扇门。
lines.textEn: Without a solid reputation in Tarkov, Lightkeeper won't even consider meeting you in person. You haven't built up enough trust to get your foot in the door.

lines.textCh: 我该怎么解决这个问题？
lines.textEn: How do I fix that?

lines.textCh: 不要轻易拒接其他商人派来的差事，不光要快些办完，还得办好。 如果你能努力活下来，完成差事，赢得所有人的尊重，那么和 Lightkeeper 合作的机会也许就会找上门来。
lines.textEn: Don't turn down work from the traders, and do it well. If you survive and earn everyone's respect, you'll at least have a chance of working with Lightkeeper.

lines.textCh: 如果连关于他的这些情报都能挖到，那你在塔科夫还是挺混得开的。
lines.textEn: You've done pretty well for yourself in Tarkov if you've managed to dig up even that much about him.

lines.textCh: 我想当面找他谈谈，该怎么才能和他见面？
lines.textEn: I want to talk to him. How do I do that?

lines.textCh: 我倒是乐意帮你这个忙…… Lightkeeper 对于合作对象的选择标准一向很挑剔。尽管你已经在塔科夫的商人圈子里积累了一些名誉，但光靠这个还远远不够。
lines.textEn: I'd be glad to help you... Lightkeeper is extremely selective about who he works with. You've already built yourself a reputation as someone reliable, but that's not enough.

lines.textCh: 我还需要哪些东西？
lines.textEn: What else do I need?

lines.textCh: 除非 Lightkeeper 有求于你，否则根本没戏。
lines.textEn: Until Lightkeeper needs something from you, you don't stand a chance.

lines.textCh: 那你当初是怎么开始和他合作的呢？
lines.textEn: How did you start working with him, then?

lines.textCh: 他并没有直接找我“合作”。这家伙至多只是通过中间人从我手里买些设备而已。 你得知道，我在很久之前就试着想和 Lightkeeper 接上线了。如果真的有能接触他的机会，我会告诉你的。
lines.textEn: He doesn't work with me directly, either. At most, he buys equipment through intermediaries. But I've wanted to establish direct contact with him for a long time, too. I'll get in touch if I see an opportunity to reach Lightkeeper.

68cbcfb02cdee534ad02d212.textCh:
在突袭 TerraGroup 办公室的时候，附近的高楼顶部突然发生了一起大爆炸。我与指挥部失去了联络，只剩下我一个人了。看起来我必须得自己想办法撤离。

但首先，我必须活着离开这里——曾经繁华的中心区，如今的原爆点。
68cbcfb02cdee534ad02d212.textEn:
During the assault on the TerraGroup office, a massive explosion erupted on top of one of the nearby high-rises. I got left on my own, with no contact with command. Looks like I'll have to handle the evacuation myself.

But first things first, I have to get out of this Ground Zero.

68cbdaac76fe74b1e80bfd98.textCh: 后备撤离点位于海边的港口区，要想到达那个地方，我必须得孤身穿过整座城市。好在为了以防万一，指挥部事先打点了几个本地联络人——他们熟悉这里的路线，需要补给也可以让他们帮忙。 为了安全穿过城市，我需要那位 Therapist 出手相助：她知道从市中心前往塔科夫街区最安全的路线，独自冒险探查路线并不是好主意，现在孤身一人的情况下更是如此。我需要 Therapist 的情报，况且如果能和这样一位重要线人接上头，之后的行动也许会顺利些。 或者我也可以绕过市区，直接前往通向港口区的高速公路立交桥。但那里是 Ragman 的地盘，如果要穿过那里，就必须想办法先和他见面。 我可以试着与 Therapist 与 Ragman 合作，同时前往立交桥打探情况。
68cbdaac76fe74b1e80bfd98.textEn: The backup evacuation point is located at the port on the coast, but reaching it means moving straight through the city. In case of an emergency, command left us a few local contacts — people who know the routes and can help with supplies. To get through the city streets, I'll need help from a certain Therapist. She knows the safe approaches to the Streets of Tarkov, and without her intel, heading in would be too risky. She might also be a valuable contact down the line. I could also bypass the downtown area and head for the highway interchange that leads toward the port. But that area is under Ragman's watch. I’ll have to make arrangements with him first if I want to pass through. I can try working with Therapist and Ragman, and also make my way to the interchange.

68cc0dae2bdcc15c010c2673.textCh: Therapist 说她可以安排路线让我能安全撤离，但她的服务并不免费。虽然不知道应不应该相信她，但眼下我别无选择，我得想办法搜罗些现金来。
68cc0dae2bdcc15c010c2673.textEn: Therapist said she can secure safe exit routes, but it's gonna cost. I'm not sure I can trust her, but there's no other option. I need to gather the cash.

68cc0ec72cdee534ad02d2e8.textCh: Therapist 为我安排了一条安全通道，成功穿过了市区。 现在我可以自由 前往塔科夫街区 了。
68cc0ec72cdee534ad02d2e8.textEn: Therapist has provided me with safe routes through the city blocks. I can now access streets of Tarkov when needed.

68cc0f7ddabf984a73078e46.textCh: 出乎我的意料，Ragman 相当随和，道理也讲得通。虽然他没立刻放行，不过我只要为他干个简单的差事就能通过。他还愿意把我介绍给海关航站楼地区的某个本地大佬。至少目前有点进展了，还算不坏。
68cc0f7ddabf984a73078e46.textEn: Ragman turned out to be a pretty reasonable person. He's not letting me through for free, but in exchange for a simple job, he's willing to introduce me to one of the local big shots over by the customs terminal. That's something, at least.

68cc0f9ddabf984a73078e49.textCh: 我和 Ragman 做了笔交易，可以继续从立交桥前往港口了。如果真的据传言所说，港口区被严密封锁了起来，我还得依靠他这样的本地联络人才能继续前进。 Ragman 承诺他会把我介绍给当地一个叫 Skier 的商人，也许我应该去会会这个地头蛇。 我现在可以前往海关，以及与 Skier 合作 了。要想抵达港口，这是唯一的办法。
68cc0f9ddabf984a73078e49.textEn: I managed to make a deal with Ragman for safe passage from the Interchange towards the Terminal. If the port really is sealed off, I'll need contacts like him. Ragman promised to introduce me to a local trader who goes by the name Skier. I should pay him a visit. I can now move into customs and start working with Skier. It's the only way I'll reach the port.

68cc3a70e807a020390484b0.textCh: Skier 认识化工厂附近的某个武器专家，能和这么重要的商人搭上线，这种机会我可不敢轻易错过。但 Skier 也开了价：他要我收集建筑材料帮他重建仓库，才能把武器商的情报给我。
68cc3a70e807a020390484b0.textEn: Skier knows some kind of weapons specialist near the chemical plant. That's not the kind of contact I can afford to pass up. But in exchange for the info, Skier wants me to help gather building materials to rebuild one of his warehouses.

68cc3a8aca620f42260128c2.textCh: Skier 为我指明了前往 工厂 的路线，甚至还给了我 联系 Mechanic 的方式。 Mechanic 也许算得上塔科夫本地最炙手可热的商人了，每个雇佣兵都想从他那定制装备。我得赶快安排时间见他，越快越好。
68cc3a8aca620f42260128c2.textEn: Skier pointed me the way to the factory and even gave me a contact to link up with Mechanic. Mechanic could turn out to be one of the most valuable contacts in Tarkov. I need to make this meeting happen soon.

68cc3ad4ca620f42260128c5.textCh:
当整个世界都陷入疯狂时，Mechanic 是塔科夫为数不多还保留着人性面孔的存在。他愿意帮我联系 Prapor，本地俄制武器最主要的供应来源。

但在我出发去见 Prapor 之前，Mechanic 想让我帮他做件事。我得去侦察一下工厂的最新情况，和盘踞在那里的本地强盗们打个照面。Mechanic 要我弄几件这些人使用的武器来，好搞清楚到底是谁给他们提供装备，伺机攻下化工厂。
68cc3ad4ca620f42260128c5.textEn:
Mechanic is one of the few who's still trying to keep a human face in Tarkov. He's willing to put me in touch with Prapor, who has supply channels for Russian weapons.

But before he sends me, he asked a favor. I need to recon the Factory and find the bandits holed up there. Mechanic wants samples of their weaponry to determine exactly who's planning to seize the Factory.

68cc3aef14a6ef850b051c67.textCh: 通往港口的路从工厂出发，一直穿过 Priozersk 自然保护区，也就是本地的森林地区。Mechanic 不仅分享了几条安全路线，还把 Prapor 的联系方式给了我，这样就能稳定弄到俄国产的武器装备了。 现在 我可以前往森林地区，并与 Prapor 进行合作。
68cc3aef14a6ef850b051c67.textEn: The road to the port runs from the Factory through the Priozersk nature reserve, and Mechanic shared a couple of routes with me along with a contact for Prapor, who can provide me with Russian-made equipment. Now I can access the woods area and start working with Prapor.

68cc3b532e3838784e00a2ad.textCh: Skier 这回给了个更难的差事。我得在森林保护区里大闹一番，把骚扰 Skier 仓库的那些 Scav 给消灭掉。不过好消息是我不用自己追查这件事的来龙去脉。对于 Skier 那个滑头来说，闹出点动静就足够了。
68cc3b532e3838784e00a2ad.textEn: This time Skier gave me a tougher job. I need to stir up trouble in the nature reserve and neutralize the Scavs that attacked Skier's warehouses. I don’t necessarily have to track down anyone specific. For Skier, the point is to make a loud statement.

68cc3b5bb5a3172cff09466a.textCh: 我把 Skier 要办的事都搞定了，作为回报，他给我标出了通往海边的路线。据说在撤离行动期间，“蔚蓝海岸”疗养院曾经是一处重要的 TerraGroup 集结点与中转站。 现在 我可以前往海岸线 了，我还能 从 Peacekeeper 那里购买装备。
68cc3b5bb5a3172cff09466a.textEn: I completed the job for Skier, and in return he showed me a path to the coast. They say the Azure Coast health resort was an important TerraGroup point during the evacuation. Now I can access shoreline, and I can also buy equipment from Peacekeeper.

68cc3bc51aa5b98826038e10.textCh: 现在我终于能来到海岸边，亲眼看看港口区的那个撤离点了——港口肯定有重兵把守，但守军应该会在门外留有某种通讯设备，对讲机什么的，好让里面的人知道是自己人。如果这个想法没错的话，我得找到那个地方，想办法和港口的守军联系。
68cc3bc51aa5b98826038e10.textEn: I can now get to the coast and investigate the evacuation point at the port terminal. The port must be guarded, but the military likely left some kind of comms to contact them from outside the gate. I need to find it and make contact with the garrison at the port.

68cc3bcce807a020390484b5.textCh:
港口确实完全封锁起来了。他们非常干脆地叫我滚蛋，看样子是不打算放任何人进去。或许还有其他路线能逃出塔科夫，但从头开始寻找线索无异于大海捞针。

也就是说，我得找个藏身处安顿下来从长计议，想办法与本地的商人们增进联系。出路越多，消息来得更快，逃出这里的希望也就越大。
68cc3bcce807a020390484b5.textEn:
The port is indeed sealed off. They told me to get lost, and it doesn't look like they're letting anyone through at all.

There’s still no contact with command, but that doesn’t necessarily mean anything. I doubt they’d abandon this many trained fighters in Tarkov. Either way, staying put without checking the evacuation point would’ve been a mistake.

I need to talk to the locals. That might be my best chance of getting out of here.

68cc3ce62e3838784e00a2b0.textCh:
通过 Mechanic，我联系上了在灯塔附近海岸执行任务的 Peacekeeper。但他执意要我“资助”本地的 UN 维和部队，否则就拒绝进行进一步接触——这基本意味着只有照他的要求办才能换来通往灯塔的安全之路。

看样子我必须花钱才能买到一条通路，之后也得靠他才能搞到西方装备。这笔钱得通过 Mechanic 交到他手上。
68cc3ce62e3838784e00a2b0.textEn:
Through Mechanic I managed to get in touch with Peacekeeper, who operates on the coast around the Tarkov lighthouse. Without an "investment" in the UNTAR operation, Peacekeeper refuses to give a safe route to him.

Looks like I'll have to pay for the ability to move freely in that area and to gain access to Western gear. The money has to be delivered through Mechanic.

68cc3ff71e25f65955034a2d.textCh: 我现在可以 前往灯塔 了。尽管我现在对细节还知之甚少，但是看样子在封锁之下的塔科夫，Peacekeeper 算得上是最有权势的那一批人。
68cc3ff71e25f65955034a2d.textEn: I can now make my way to the lighthouse. I still don't know the details, but it seems one of the most influential people in locked-down Tarkov is there.

68cc40541e25f65955034a30.textCh: 有人在海岸线疗养院附近袭击了 Prapor 的车队。从对方使用的武器来看，显然是 PMC 干的。现在 Prapor 彻底怒了，发誓要找到袭击背后的真凶。他说对方干完这一票之后带着战利品肯定走不远，只有给他带来 PMC 的狗牌，才能告诉我前往军事基地的道路。
68cc40541e25f65955034a30.textEn: Someone attacked Prapor's convoy on the coast near the health resort. Judging by their weapons, the attackers were clearly PMC operatives. Now Prapor wants to find out exactly who was behind the attack. He said they couldn't have gone far and is demanding PMC dogtags in exchange for the route to some military base.

68cc405a25e85c29cb0461cb.textCh: 作为回报，Prapor 给了我本地驻军储备基地的坐标。这种储备基地里一般都存放着大量装备和补给，也许还能从记录中知道塔科夫到底都发生了些什么。 我现在可以前往储备站了。
68cc405a25e85c29cb0461cb.textEn: In exchange for the favor, Prapor gave me the coordinates of a local Russian military reserve base. The base could hold a lot of important supplies and data on what's happening in Tarkov. I can now access the reserve.

68cc40932e3838784e00a2b5.textCh:
早在被派来塔科夫之前，我就听不少战友提到城市地底下埋藏着某种 TerraGroup 的神秘设施。如果传言是真的，那么里面应该还有不少重要的样本，或者集团的绝密实验数据。要是我能搞到 TerraGroup 的机密，绝对能换来一张回家的船票。当地人还是三缄其口，不让我掺和他们的调查，我只能靠自己去发掘真相了。

没有线索的话，我根本找不到 TerraGroup 的远程控制站点。但他们肯定会在城市里设置实验中心或者类似的其他设施。而我得先找到入口，才能想办法进去。

对于这种级别的设施，TerraGroup 肯定设立了严密的通行权限系统，我必须找到对应的钥匙卡或密码才行。
68cc40932e3838784e00a2b5.textEn:
Even before being sent to Tarkov, many of our guys were talking about some underground TerraGroup facilities. Maybe if I can grab a truly important sample or some real data from there, I'll have a better shot at getting out of the city. The locals still won't trust me with anything important. I have to act on my own.

I won't be able to find TerraGroup's remote sites without a lead. But they must have had a hub or some facility inside the city. I need to find the entrance and figure out how to break in.

For a site like that, TerraGroup probably set up an access system, meaning I can’t get in without a specific keycard or access codes.

68cc409aca620f42260128ce.textCh: 我成功进入了 TerraGroup 的地下实验室。我需要彻底搜查这个地方，弄清楚这里的具体方位和其他情况。
68cc409aca620f42260128ce.textEn: I managed to get into an underground TerraGroup laboratory. I need to thoroughly search the interior and get my bearings here.

68cc40a2b5a3172cff094670.textCh: 我找到了深埋在街区之下的 TerraGroup 秘密设施——不是狭小逼仄的地下室，而是设施齐备的一整个实验室……看样子 TerraGroup Labs 把大多数见不得人的研究项目都转移到这里进行了。设施里的许多大门都用电子锁紧闭着，可能需要不同通行权限的钥匙卡才能打开。 等发掘出更多消息之后，我会再回来的，也许需要探索多次才能完全弄清楚这里的状况。但首先，我必须弄到更好的装备才行。 不管怎么样，现在我 可以前往实验室 了。
68cc40a2b5a3172cff094670.textEn: I found not just a TerraGroup basement room under the city blocks, but a full-fledged underground laboratory... It looks like this is where the main work of TerraGroup Labs was done. Many doors are locked with keycards at different access levels. I'm going to have to come back here, and more than once. But first I need to score better gear. In any case, now I can access the lab.

68cc41151e25f65955034a34.textCh: Prapor 提到的那个“门票”似乎就是逃出塔科夫的关键了。我必须抓住这个机会，不能让它白白跑掉，就算耗费再多的时间与精力也是值得的。
68cc41151e25f65955034a34.textEn: It seems the ticket Prapor mentioned might be the key to escaping Tarkov. I can’t afford to waste this opportunity, even if it takes lots of time and effort.

68cc411ce807a020390484bb.textCh:
港口的撤离行动已被叫停，但我想办法弄清了我现在所处的方位坐标，以及通往几乎每个地区相对安全的路线。我还结识了几个愿意和我合作的商人。

眼下要做的是继续与当地人建立关系，我必须成为他们之间必不可少的一环，毕竟来日方长。
68cc411ce807a020390484bb.textEn:
The evacuation at the port has been shut down. But I've managed to get my bearings in Tarkov and now know safe approaches to almost every district. I've also met several traders who are willing to work with me.

I should keep building bridges and shoring up my position, because it's going to be a long time before I get out of here.

68cc6b5a7d70b6a2ec06b2ac.textCh: 在自然保护区，我发现了一架迫降在森林里的飞机——准确来说，只剩下支离破碎的残骸了。飞上天的东西总归是要落地的，但面对眼前这堆扭曲的金属碎片，我实在难以想象他们到底经历了什么。我该去问问商人们，也许他们会知道相关的消息。我总有种预感：这架飞机的背后并不是单纯的事故那么简单。
68cc6b5a7d70b6a2ec06b2ac.textEn: In the nature reserve, I came across a downed plane — or rather, what's left of it. I couldn't tell why it went down after looking at the wreckage. I should ask around with the traders, maybe someone knows more. I've got a strong feeling this plane is important.

68cc6b94be134906dc0f3c3b.textCh: Prapor 打发我去一辆 G 型越野车里找一个 U 盘，我只要找出那辆倒霉越野车的位置就行了。他说 Therapist 可能知道相关情况，也许我该去问问医生女士。
68cc6b94be134906dc0f3c3b.textEn: Prapor sent me to find a flash drive in a G-Wagon. Now I just need to figure out where exactly it is. He said Therapist knows something about this. I should pay her a visit.

68cc6bae09674594fc070ee6.textCh: 我找到了 U 盘，现在只需要把它带到 Prapor 那就行了。希望之后他能告诉我里面装的是什么。
68cc6bae09674594fc070ee6.textEn: I found the flash drive. Now I need to get it to Prapor. Hopefully, he'll tell me what's on it later.

68cc6bb425e85c29cb046211.textCh: 完事了，现在 U 盘已经送到了 Prapor 手里。等他看过里面的东西，我就能得到消息了。
68cc6bb425e85c29cb046211.textEn: All done, the flash drive is now with Prapor. I'll have to wait until he's gone through all the data and calls me in.

68cc6bceb5a3172cff0946b5.textCh: Therapist 的线人提出要用美元支付报酬，而且必须是现金。我得想办法弄到这笔钱，不然我就得自己去翻遍整个塔科夫了。
68cc6bceb5a3172cff0946b5.textEn: Therapist's informant is asking for dollars in cash. I need to bring them, unless I want to track down the vehicle on my own.

68cc6bd014a6ef850b051cb2.textCh: 我把钱交到了 Therapist 手上，她让我等她的消息。
68cc6bd014a6ef850b051cb2.textEn: I gave the cash to Therapist. She told me to wait a while.

68cc6bd91aa5b98826038e5a.textCh: Therapist 的线人回话了：“在塌方隧道周围，一辆黑色的大 G 越野车”。
68cc6bd91aa5b98826038e5a.textEn: Therapist's informant sent her a message: "Look for a black G-Wagon near the blown-out tunnel".

68cc6c1b5c3b43c0330444a1.textCh: 我没去拜托 Therapist ，也没问那个线人，而是自己搞定了一切。Therapist 只说会转告那个线人，他的情报已经过时了。
68cc6c1b5c3b43c0330444a1.textEn: I managed to find everything without Therapist or her informant. She said she’ll let her contact know that his info is outdated.

68cc6c1c25e85c29cb046214.textCh: U 盘里的文件证明了那架客机并非意外坠毁在自然保护区内，而是被人击落的。Prapor 派我前去回收机上的飞行记录仪，应该能揭露当时到底发生了什么。
68cc6c1c25e85c29cb046214.textEn: The flash drive revealed that the plane in the nature reserve was shot down deliberately. Prapor sent me to find the flight recorder. It should help shed light on what really happened there.

68cc6c4009674594fc070ee9.textCh: 我把飞行记录仪放在了指定的地方，现在只需要等待解密结果就好。希望里面记录的内容值得我折腾这么一趟。
68cc6c4009674594fc070ee9.textEn: I left the flight recorder in place. Now all that’s left is to wait for the decryption results. Hopefully, it’ll be worth all this running around.

68cc6c40661b151789017c37.textCh: 我找到了飞行记录仪，Elektronik 会负责进行解密。但我得把东西送到指定的地方交货才行——就在海岸线的 Scav 钓鱼小岛上，岛上一角的房间里。
68cc6c40661b151789017c37.textEn: I found the box. Elektronik will decrypt it, but I need to leave it on the fishing island at the coast, in the corner room.

68cc6c68410c3a0f300e2bc4.textCh: 我把 Prapor 要的东西都给他了，现在只能等待结果。
68cc6c68410c3a0f300e2bc4.textEn: I’ve handed over everything Prapor needs. Now all that’s left is to wait.

68cc6c68e807a020390484fc.textCh:
Prapor 联系了我，叫我过去一趟。依然没能收获任何有用的情报，只是又给我派了个活。但如果我想继续接近真相，就必须完成这单差事。

他给了我一张破译飞行记录仪所需设备的清单，我得把这些东西都找齐了，否则 Elektronik 就没法破解黑匣子。
68cc6c68e807a020390484fc.textEn:
Prapor contacted me and called me over. I didn’t get any useful info, just another task. But I have to complete it if I want to get to the truth.

He gave me a list of everything he needs. I have to bring it all to him, otherwise Elektronik won’t be able to decrypt the flight recorder.

68cc6c8f1aa5b98826038e5e.textCh:
又是这样，Prapor 没提供任何信息，反而又给我布置了另一项任务。

我需要取回 U 盘，以及客机机组对话记录的打印件。Elektronik 已经把它们留在了约定好的地方。
68cc6c8f1aa5b98826038e5e.textEn:
Once again, instead of any info, Prapor gave me another task.

I need to retrieve the flash drive and a transcript printout of the plane crew conversations. Elektronik left them at the agreed-upon location.

68cc6c8f7d70b6a2ec06b2b1.textCh: 我找到了打印出来的文件，虽然花了好些功夫才找到 Elektronik 的藏匿点，但应该还算值得。
68cc6c8f7d70b6a2ec06b2b1.textEn: I found the transcript. It took a while to find Elektronik's stash, but it was worth it.

68cc6ca5410c3a0f300e2bc7.textCh: 我拿到了 U 盘，现在只剩下最后一步了。
68cc6ca5410c3a0f300e2bc7.textEn: I have the flash drive. Now's the final step.

68cc6ca5e807a020390484ff.textCh: 就在 Prapor 开始读那堆文件的时候，突然有人打电话给他——显然这通电话来自某个大人物，要么就是什么机密事项。他直接把我轰出去了，我得等他处理完手头的事才行。
68cc6ca5e807a020390484ff.textEn: Prapor started reading the transcript, and at that moment someone called him — clearly about something important. He kicked me out. I’ll have to wait until he’s dealt with his business.

68cc6cbd09674594fc070eec.textCh:
结果 Prapor 接到的那通电话是 Kerman 先生打来的！和机组最后的语音记录里提到的是同一个人！这背后肯定有什么见不得人的东西……

Prapor 命令我重新返回飞机坠毁现场找一个加固手提箱——他和那个 Kerman 先生管那个箱子叫“门票”。Prapor 要我找到箱子后立刻带回来给他……也许可以另作打算……？但现在下决定未免太早了。
68cc6cbd09674594fc070eec.textEn:
Turns out Prapor got a call from Mr. Kerman! It's the same guy mentioned in the transcript. Something shady is going on…

Prapor said I need to find an armored case near the plane crash site. He — and this Mr. Kerman — call it the "Ticket". After that, I’m supposed to bring the case to Prapor. Unless… Well, I haven’t decided yet.

68cc6cbd661b151789017c3a.textCh: 我在森林坠机现场找到了那个箱子，就这种程度的事故来说，保存得还算完好。现在我得拿定主意，接下来到底该怎么处置它。
68cc6cbd661b151789017c3a.textEn: I found the case near the plane crash site. It’s pretty well preserved. Now I need to decide what to do with it next.

68cc6cd3be134906dc0f3c3e.textCh: 我决定信守诺言，把箱子交给 Prapor。最好还是不要轻易招惹这个地头蛇。
68cc6cd3be134906dc0f3c3e.textEn: I chose not to double‑cross Prapor and gave him the armored case. It's best not to mess with people like him.

68cc6cd3e807a02039048502.textCh:
这个 Kerman 是很阴险，但 Prapor 的手段比那个神秘人要狠毒一百倍，所以我最终决定自己留着箱子，看看到底是什么名堂。他们不约而同管这东西叫“门票”肯定不是毫无依据的。如果这对于他们来说意义重大，那么我自然也能用它换来一张回家的船票。至于翻脸之后怎么和 Prapor 修复关系……到时候自然会有办法。

我有预感，Kerman 肯定很快就会再次联系我。我最好还是静观其变。
68cc6cd3e807a02039048502.textEn:
This Mr. Kerman is shady, sure, but Prapor’s even shadier, so I decided to keep the case for myself. This "Ticket" isn’t called that for nothing. I figure I can use it to get out of Tarkov. As for my rep with Prapor… I’ll manage.

Also, I have a feeling Kerman is going to contact me soon. It's best I stay put.

68cc6e50be134906dc0f3c42.textCh: 我发现了 Kerman 留下的消息。他到底是怎么进来的？还是说，是别人替他写的条子……？无论如何，显然他并不希望我把箱子就这么交给 Prapor。我得好好想想，分析分析前后利害才行。
68cc6e50be134906dc0f3c42.textEn: I found a note from Kerman. How did he even manage to get it here? Or did someone write it for him…? Either way, he clearly doesn’t want me to give the case to Prapor. I need to think this through.

68dfaad6006f2cb41709d8c6.textCh: 我和 Mechanic 聊到了坠毁在森林自然保护区里的那架飞机。没人清楚那天飞机上到底发生了什么，也许我该追查到底——说不定会有什么有意思的发现。
68dfaad6006f2cb41709d8c6.textEn: Mechanic and I got to talking about that plane that went down somewhere in the nature reserve. Nobody really knows what happened to it. I should track it down and take a look — maybe I’ll find something interesting.

68e4e999793f60590607f951.textCh: Kerman 先生，也就是飞行员最后语音记录里提到的那个神秘人，想和我谈谈。为了和他搭上线，我得弄一台笔记本来，还得搞好网络连接——光有这些还不够，我还得搞一台发电机来为整个藏身处提供稳定的电力，灯也该换个像样点的。但在此之前，我得把藏身处的门给加固牢了，免得随便什么人闯进来把这里洗劫一空。说到底，我必须把这里收拾成能住人的样子——显然，我还得在这待上一阵子。
68e4e999793f60590607f951.textEn: Mr. Kerman, the one from the transcript, wants to talk. For that I need a laptop and a comms setup, I can’t just find it and set it up in an empty room. I’ll need a solid generator so the power doesn’t cut out, proper lighting, and I’ll have to reinforce the Hideout door so nobody breaks in. Bottom line, I need to make this place livable — I’m clearly stuck here for a while.

68e4e9fbead7751ba5066eae.textCh: Kerman 先生，就是黑匣子记录里提到的那个神秘人，像训小屁孩一样把我批得体无完肤，还说这下我是别想逃出塔科夫了。鬼才会信他的屁话，箱子在我手里，我看这个 Kerman 一定是必有所求。最好等上一段时间，等他冷静下来之后再谈。
68e4e9fbead7751ba5066eae.textEn: Mr. Kerman, the one mentioned in the transcript, chewed me out like a kid and said there’s no way I’m getting out of Tarkov now. That’s bullshit. I think Kerman wants something from me. I’ll give him a bit of time to cool off.

68e4ea0a39667d2d6c00453a.textCh: Kerman 大费周章和我接上线肯定不是为了过嘴瘾这么简单，他肯定想从我这得到什么。等冷静下来之后，他大概会再找过来的。
68e4ea0a39667d2d6c00453a.textEn: Kerman didn’t reach out just to chew me out. He needs something. I’m guessing he’ll get back to me once he cools down.

68e4ea4adcd893159e09261d.textCh: Kerman 再次联系上了我，告诉我最好还是把那个箱子还回去。还真是谢谢你啊，大聪明先生，能不能说点我不知道的东西？！看来我只能回去找 Prapor 了，但愿他不会因为之前的过节漫天要价。
68e4ea4adcd893159e09261d.textEn: Kerman got in touch with me again. He says the case needs to be brought back. Thanks, mister obvious! I need to see Prapor. Hopefully, he won’t try to overcharge.

68e4ea5c793f60590607f954.textCh:
完了，Prapor 让我滚蛋，现在真的走投无路了。

既然如此，我只能和 Kerman 合作了，我应该找他把所有事情都好好梳理一遍。
68e4ea5c793f60590607f954.textEn:
Prapor told me to go screw myself. I’m at a dead end.

I should go over everything with Kerman, now that we’re working together.

68e4ea6f36a9240a3704e7ba.textCh:
Kerman 给了我搜寻地点的线索，虽然我没指望能有什么新发现，但总得试试吧。

据 Kerman 说，Prapor 手下在距离那座灯塔不远的地方扎营。就从那里开始搜索吧。
68e4ea6f36a9240a3704e7ba.textEn:
Kerman gave me a lead on where to search. I’m not expecting to find anything new, but it’s worth a shot.

Kerman said Prapor’s people were camped not far from the lighthouse. That’s where I’ll start the search.

68e4eae2ead7751ba5066eb2.textCh: 我找到了营地，看样子他们才走没多久。我还找到了一张纸条，上面写着货物送到了灯塔小岛上某个人的手里。
68e4eae2ead7751ba5066eb2.textEn: I found the camp. They left not long ago. I also found a note, which says the cargo was delivered to someone from the Lighthouse island.

68e4eaf439667d2d6c00453e.textCh: 从纸条上写的东西来看，Prapor 的手下确实是在把一件重要的货物送到灯塔里的什么人手里。我需要和 Kerman 谈谈这件事。
68e4eaf439667d2d6c00453e.textEn: Judging by the note, Prapor’s people really were passing something important to someone at the lighthouse. I need to discuss this with Kerman.

68e4eb2f2411dc8de20ba1ae.textCh:
Kerman 相当确定纸条里提到的就是我要的那个箱子。他还说我应该想办法和 Lightkeeper 见一面，而这个神秘人就驻扎在灯塔里——还真是人如其名啊。

可能 Prapor 的手下带给那个 Lightkeeper 的就是我的“门票”箱子。我必须和他谈谈——说不定我们能达成某种合作。
68e4eb2f2411dc8de20ba1ae.textEn:
Kerman is certain that the note is about the case I need. He also said I have to arrange a meeting with Lightkeeper, who is, unexpectedly, stationed at the lighthouse.

Chances are, Prapor’s people handed the Ticket case over to Lightkeeper. I need to talk to him — maybe we can come to an agreement.

68e4eb602411dc8de20ba1b2.textCh: Lightkeeper 没有马上让我滚蛋，这倒是出乎意料。他说只要我为他干活，就可以拿到那个箱子，但我总有种预感，这样的差事绝对麻烦少不了……
68e4eb602411dc8de20ba1b2.textEn: Lightkeeper didn’t kick me out right away, which is something. He said he’ll trade the case for my work, but I can’t shake the feeling that the tasks are going to be brutal.

68e4eb6c36a9240a3704e7be.textCh: Lightkeeper 又给了我一个差事，希望之后别再有其他麻烦了。
68e4eb6c36a9240a3704e7be.textEn: Lightkeeper gave me another task. Hopefully, this is the last one.

68e4eb83793f60590607f95a.textCh: Lightkeeper 说，我只要“吸引注意力”就行了——他八成说的是发射信号弹。听起来，他想把人给引出来，然后让我动手解决。除此之外，他没再透露更多细节。
68e4eb83793f60590607f95a.textEn: Lightkeeper said I need to "draw some attention". Most likely, he means firing a signal flare. Sounds like he wants to lure someone out and have me do the killing. He didn’t give me any more details.

68e4ebe1793f60590607f960.textCh: 不出我所料，差事果然是后一种——大开杀戒。无论如何，箱子终于到我手里了！但眼下想要庆祝还为时过早。我逃离塔科夫的路途才刚刚开始。
68e4ebe1793f60590607f960.textEn: The job really did turn out to be the last one. The case is mine now. Finally! But it’s too early to relax. My way out of Tarkov is only just beginning.

68e4ec39a8129b137b01ccce.textCh: Kerman 答应会处理好 Prapor 那边的关系，说是之后会再联系。我总觉得，我好像亲手把自己卷进了一场罗生门式的怪圈……但转念一想，至少我为自己赢得了逃出塔科夫的门票，所以大概也不全是坏事。
68e4ec39a8129b137b01ccce.textEn: Kerman promised to handle things with Prapor, and said he’d be in touch again later. I’ve got a feeling I’ve gotten myself into some weird shit… On the other hand, I’m holding a Ticket out of Tarkov, so it’s not all bad.

68e4ec6b2411dc8de20ba1b5.textCh: 完事，这个加固手提箱总算是给破开了。可以这么说，里面的确有一张“门票”——TerraGroup 签发给克鲁格洛夫的钥匙卡，以及配套的说明书。现在我得搞清楚接下来要做什么。
68e4ec6b2411dc8de20ba1b5.textEn: Done, the armored case is unlocked. There really was a ticket inside, if you can even call it that: a keycard registered to someone named Kruglov and an instruction sheet. Now I need to figure out what to do next.

68e4ecc0793f60590607f967.textCh: 每个人提到这个箱子的时候都说，里面装着逃离塔科夫的门票。我试过撬开它，但显然箱子比我想象得要更牢固，至于用枪之类的强行弄开又太过冒险——说不定里面装着什么重要的东西呢？还是找个专业人士想想办法吧，我知道有个合适的人选——我得去找 Mechanic。
68e4ecc0793f60590607f967.textEn: Everyone says the case holds a Ticket out of Tarkov. I tried to pry it open, but couldn’t. Busting it open feels too risky — what if there’s something crucial inside? Better find someone who can open it properly. And I actually know who can help. I need to go see Mechanic.

68e4ecc92411dc8de20ba1b8.textCh: Mechanic 把我请了出去。显然，在赢得他的尊重之前，我根本指望不上他。
68e4ecc92411dc8de20ba1b8.textEn: Mechanic sent me packing. He’s clearly not going to help until I earn his respect.

68e4ed1336a9240a3704e7c2.textCh: 我和 Mechanic 说了箱子的事情，他没时间亲自帮我这个忙，只说我完全可以自己找来合适的工具打开它。不过他答应了，只要我弄到所有东西，他会告诉我怎么破开箱子。
68e4ed1336a9240a3704e7c2.textEn: I talked with Mechanic. He won’t open the case for me. Says I can do it myself if I find the right tools for the job. He promised to give me the instructions once I’ve got everything ready.

68e4ed2239667d2d6c004542.textCh: 虽然花了点功夫，但干扰器毕竟是到手了。
68e4ed2239667d2d6c004542.textEn: Took some effort, but the jammer is now mine.

68e4ed2e2411dc8de20ba1bb.textCh: Mechanic 发来了破解箱子的步骤说明。我可以在工作台尝试自己动手，但需要的东西不止一个干扰器。我得想办法搞齐所有材料才行。
68e4ed2e2411dc8de20ba1bb.textEn: Mechanic sent instructions on how to open the armored case. I can do it at my workbench, but it’ll take more than just a jammer. I need to gather the rest of the materials.

68e4edd415f50c2d8603216f.textCh: 我得和那个 Kerman 谈谈，是他把我卷进来的，他应该知道下一步该干什么。
68e4edd415f50c2d8603216f.textEn: I need to get in touch with Mr. Kerman. He dragged me into this, so he probably knows what to do next.

68e4edde61ed7c6558080a4c.textCh: 我决定顺着 Kerman 的线索继续查下去。他显然知道的比他表现出来的要多，现在这正对我有利。我得靠他的情报逃出塔科夫。
68e4edde61ed7c6558080a4c.textEn: I decided to follow Kerman's lead. He clearly knows more than he lets on, and right now that's working in my favor. This is how I'll get out of Tarkov.

68e4ede761ed7c6558080a4f.textCh: Kerman 肯定有着自己的算盘，我可不想被他玩弄于股掌之中，在像个卒子一样任他驱使。既然我已经有了那张说明书，和配套的钥匙卡，我完全可以自己行动。现在我只需要前往港口就能离开这个鬼地方了。
68e4ede761ed7c6558080a4f.textEn: Kerman’s up to something, and I don’t want to be a pawn in his games. I’ll get out on my own, especially since there’s an instruction sheet with the keycard. Now I need to make my way to the port to evacuate.

68e4f261306926af9602c9e7.textCh: 就是这样了，现在距离逃出塔科夫只剩下最后的一步之遥。等到真正离开这座城市的时候，我会不会反而心生怀念之情？我不知道，但问题的答案现在已经不重要了。眼前的目标只有一个：赶到港口，完成撤离。
68e4f261306926af9602c9e7.textEn: This is it. One last push, and I’ll be out of Tarkov. I’m not sure if I’ll even miss it, but that doesn’t matter right now. The main thing is to get to the port and evacuate.

68e4ff19809d67185506e033.textCh: 终于，这个花哨的锁被破解开了。箱子就这么横放在桌子上，在一片狼藉中显得格格不入，但就在我准备打开它的瞬间，一股别样的感情涌上心头——这个箱子承载了无数希望，不知有多少人为了它而白白送命。但假如里面什么也没有呢？假如经历了一切之后真的是一场空呢？
68e4ff19809d67185506e033.textEn: I finally managed to unlock this fancy lock. I should open the case sitting on my desk among all the junk, but a weird feeling is holding me back. What if it’s empty? What if it was all for nothing?

68f3e88308c5ee28eb085d7b.textCh: Prapor 并不信任我，要想得到他的帮助，我必须赢得他的信赖才行。
68f3e88308c5ee28eb085d7b.textEn: Prapor doesn’t trust me. He clearly won’t be helping until I’ve earned his respect.

68f3e894364d40d64703b4e0.textCh: 我已经成功提升了自己在 Prapor 那的声誉，现在我可以继续处理那架飞机残骸的事情了。
68f3e894364d40d64703b4e0.textEn: I’ve improved my standing with Prapor. Now I can return to the matter of the downed plane.

68ffff4e3335c4199504704e.textCh:
早在突袭 TerraGroup 办公室之前，我就听说过他们在塔科夫的地下设施。

他们说，几个月前在海岸线的疗养院下面，有人发现了一个防空洞，或者甚至是另一个实验室——“迷宫”……我肯定得去调查一下那里，也许能进一步了解 TerraGroup 的目的。

但首先我得收集一些情报。商人们应该知道点什么。
68ffff4e3335c4199504704e.textEn:
Even before the raid on the TerraGroup office, I’d heard about their underground sites in Tarkov.

They say that under the coastal Health Reasort, a few months back, they found either a bomb shelter or another lab — "The Labyrinth"... I should definitely check that place, maybe I can learn more about what TerraGroup was up to.

But first I need to dig up some intel. The traders should know something.

68ffff5ffa562d9f24018a6b.textCh: Jaeger 说如果我能找到那支在里面失踪的 BEAR 小队的情报，他就会帮忙让我能进到“迷宫”里。我同意了。现在我需要等上几天，再去找 Jaeger 确认。到那时他应该会有关于 Knossos 门禁卡的新情报。
68ffff5ffa562d9f24018a6b.textEn: Jaeger said he’ll help with access to The Labyrinth if I can find info on the BEAR squad that went missing there. I agreed. Now I need to wait and check back with Jaeger in a couple days. By then he should have new info about the Knossos keycards.

68ffff6cbe226570590ca28a.textCh: Therapist拒绝帮忙。我得想别的办法来获取Knossos门禁卡。
68ffff6cbe226570590ca28a.textEn: Therapist refused to help. I’ll have to find another way to get the Knossos keycards.

68ffff7d3caa9d0cab08fc99.textCh:
Jaeger 的朋友正在试图查明那支在撤离期间突入“迷宫”的 BEAR 小队到底遭遇什么。这支队伍完成了他们的行动，但之后所有联络都中断了，“迷宫”也随之被封锁。作为提供 Knossos 门禁卡的条件，Jaeger 要我查出他们当时的情况。我得仔细搜索“迷宫”里的所有通道，并弄清楚这支队伍上一次突袭之后到底发生了什么。

这干起来并不容易，但我能更好地了解整个地下建筑群，还能有机会挖出 TerraGroup 秘密研究的内情。所以还是值得冒险的，况且，我办成这件差事还能提升我在 Jaeger 那里的声望。他给了我一张 Knossos 门禁卡，应该能打开“迷宫”的入口。整座 TerraGroup 秘密地下设施，以及里面蕴藏着的所有罪恶，将在我的面前轰然洞开。
68ffff7d3caa9d0cab08fc99.textEn:
Jaeger’s friend is trying to learn what happened to the BEAR squad that stormed The Labyrinth during the evacuation. The team completed their operation, but then all contact went dead and The Labyrinth was sealed. In exchange for the Knossos keycards, Jaeger wants me to find out what happened to them. I’ll have to carefully sweep all the passages in The Labyrinth and figure out what went on after the assault.

It’s not an easy job, but I’ll get a better understanding of the complex and a chance to dig up TerraGroup research. So it’s worth doing, and it’ll help build my rep with Jaeger. He gave me a Knossos keycard that should open The Labyrinth entrance. The way into the TerraGroup complex is now open.

68ffff8e70ea9e50ee0c9f30.textCh: 我把记录 BEAR 小队在“迷宫”里遭遇的那盘录音带交给了 Jaeger。这就够了，Jaeger 说他会把带子转交给他的战友。
68ffff8e70ea9e50ee0c9f30.textEn: I handed Jaeger the tape detailing what happened to the BEAR squad in The Labyrinth. That was enough, and he said he’d pass it on to his comrade.

68ffff9ab90b93f61a0cf6a2.textCh: 呼号 Leshy 的小队指挥官下令停止寻找出口，并让所有人向 #1156 项目所在的车间集合。看样子这支精英小队就这样被困在了“迷宫”里，但目前还不清楚是到底发生了什么，以及为什么他们会被困住。我需要找到这个所谓的“项目”，并调查这东西的具体情况。
68ffff9ab90b93f61a0cf6a2.textEn: The squad commander with the call sign Leshy ordered the search for exits to stop and for everyone to regroup at Item 1156. Looks like someone trapped the operatives in The Labyrinth, but it’s unclear how or why. I need to find this "Item" and check things out there.

68ffffa69f98d8e00f0ce6cf.textCh: 我没有在 #1156 项目车间里那些 BEAR 的尸体里找到 Leshy。他可能继续深入“迷宫”寻找出口了。
68ffffa69f98d8e00f0ce6cf.textEn: I didn’t find Leshy among the operatives at Item 1156. He might have continued searching for exits in The Labyrinth.

68ffffb05d8e37f04d0ae9c9.textCh: 小队指挥官命令队员在 #1156 项目车间周围设立防线。但不知为何，他自己却走出了警戒范围。他有留下了一本日志，里面应该会有更多信息。
68ffffb05d8e37f04d0ae9c9.textEn: The squad commander ordered the team to fortify at Item 1156, but for some reason, he himself went outside the perimeter. He’s got a journal, which should hold more information.

68ffffbd2f2048e6e505f0be.textCh: 看起来 TerraGroup 在“迷宫”里进行某种人体实验。当 BEAR 小队突入时，工作人员躲进了更深的地方，并打开了装着实验对象的笼子。但我既没有找到这些主管的踪影，也没有搜出任何文件。
68ffffbd2f2048e6e505f0be.textEn: It looks like TerraGroup was conducting some kind of human experiments in The Labyrinth. When the BEAR squad stormed in, the staff hid deeper inside and opened the cages with the test subjects. But I still haven’t found any of the managers or documents.

68ffffca5d8e37f04d0ae9cc.textCh: 我设法打开了那个“迷宫”高级主管把自己困在里面的办公室。他已经自杀了，但在死之前，他在一盘录音带上录下了一些东西。
68ffffca5d8e37f04d0ae9cc.textEn: I managed to open the office where the senior Labyrinth staff member had barricaded himself. He killed himself, but before dying, he recorded something on a tape.

68ffffe55b2af7f913036726.textCh: 我找到了一堆实验技术人员的笔记。它们包含了大量关于实验对象的信息。
68ffffe55b2af7f913036726.textEn: I found a bunch of notes from the lab technicians. They contain a lot of information about the test subjects.

68ffffef2f2048e6e505f0c2.textCh:
现在已经清楚 BEAR 小队在突袭期间的遭遇了。小队刚突入设施，“迷宫”里的 TerraGroup 的工作人员就封锁了所有出入口。然后那名高级研究员把笼子里的试验对象都给放了出来。就算这些人长期处于疯狂与极度疲惫的边缘，就算他们手无寸铁、没有任何战斗训练，却把所有 BEAR 队员全部残忍地杀害了。

真是太悲惨了……然而，再残酷的真相也好过继续懵懂无知。
68ffffef2f2048e6e505f0c2.textEn:
Now it’s clear what happened to the BEAR squad after the assault. Right after the team got in, the Labyrinth staff locked all the entrances and exits. Then the senior employee released the test subjects from their cages. These people had long been on the brink of madness and exhaustion, and they took out all the BEARs, even though they were unarmed and had no combat training.

A terrible fate… but knowing the truth is better than living a lie.

690000159f98d8e00f0ce6d2.textCh:
在录音带里，“迷宫”的那名高级员工说他会尽一切努力把这座设施中进行实验的报告与结果保存下来。

那名开枪自尽的工作人员说他把文件封装起来，然后给送进了下水道里。这意味着我需要到外面去找。也许“迷宫”和疗养院共用排水管线呢？也许就能在更下游的位置找到那个加密文件夹？
690000159f98d8e00f0ce6d2.textEn:
On the audio tape, the senior Labyrinth employee said he would try to preserve the reports on the experiments conducted in the complex.

The staff member who shot himself said he secured the documents and sent them into the drainage system. That means I need to search outside. Perhaps the Labyrinth and Health Resort sewers meet somewhere, and I can locate the secure folder further downstream?

690000235b2af7f913036729.textCh: 我找到了装有“迷宫”实验报告的文件夹。报告清楚地写着 TerraGroup 进行了残忍的人体实验，就算牺牲了无数的受害者也没能阻止他们的实验。看来他们为了所谓的“研究”愿意做任何事情。
690000235b2af7f913036729.textEn: I found a folder with the Labyrinth experiment reports. They explicitly state that TerraGroup carried out brutal human experiments, and countless victims didn’t stop them. Looks like they’re willing to do anything for their so-called "research".

69001c0726f726610e0e3f88.textCh:
在突袭办公室期间，有人在摩天楼顶引爆了某种特殊武器……在昏迷之前，我只记得看到了一道明亮的蓝色闪光。在此之后，所有电子设备都失效了。

我从没想过在突袭 TerraGroup 设施的时候居然会遭遇 EMP 攻击，事实上，这一高能武器本身就相当不可思议，我需要找出他们到底是用了什么技术手段袭击了城市，这一切的幕后黑手又是谁。

没有谁比Mechanic更适合帮忙处理这件事了。
69001c0726f726610e0e3f88.textEn:
During the raid on the office, some kind of special weapon went off on one of the roofs… I remember a bright blue flash before I blacked out. After that, all the electronics failed.

I’ve never encountered such a powerful EMP weapon before. I need to find out what technology hit the city, and who’s behind it.

There’s hardly anyone better to help with this than Mechanic.

69001c147e6dd507c70a57e8.textCh:
Mechanic 也不知道是什么装置在城市上空引爆了。但他确认这场爆炸的原爆点就在塔科夫市中心。

我们商量好了，我会去寻找装置的碎片，而 Mechanic 会对其进行研究，有了结果也会告诉我。除了街区和中心区之外，它几乎不可能落到别的地方。
69001c147e6dd507c70a57e8.textEn:
Mechanic doesn’t know what device went off over the city either. But he confirmed that the epicenter of the blast was the Tarkov city center.

We agreed that I’ll look for a fragment of the device, and Mechanic will study it and share the findings. There’s hardly any place it could’ve ended up besides the city streets and the ground zero.

69001c27254c6d34d1014839.textCh:
Mechanic 检查了我在中心区找到的那块碎片。看起来这是 TerraGroup 的某项技术。

为了了解更多情况，我需要在地下实验室的服务器机房连接一台局域网入侵装置。然后 Mechanic 会尝试从现存设施中任何完好的存储设备中提取更多数据。
69001c27254c6d34d1014839.textEn:
Mechanic examined the fragment I found in the city center. Looks like it’s one of TerraGroup’s technologies.

To learn more, I need to hook a LAN hacking device up in the server room of the underground lab. Then Mechanic will try to pull more data from any surviving storage.

69001c46ac1b5f4cad06e3d5.textCh: Mechanic 提出要买下我找到的那块碎片。我能靠这个东西小赚一笔没错，但同时我完全不知道 Mechanic 打算用这块碎片做什么，以及他的“研究”又会导致怎样的结果。
69001c46ac1b5f4cad06e3d5.textEn: Mechanic offered to buy the fragment I found. On one hand, I could make a decent payday. But I have no idea what Mechanic plans to do with the fragment or where his "research" will lead.

69001c513caa9d0cab08fcc5.textCh: 我决定把 #1156 装置的碎片卖给 Mechanic。不过是一块引爆过的破铜烂铁罢了，大概没什么危险的，而且有钱赚总是好的。
69001c513caa9d0cab08fcc5.textEn: I decided to sell the fragment of Item 1156 to Mechanic. This scrap probably isn’t dangerous, and cash never hurts.

69001c6cc637c00f150e3648.textCh: 我决定不把碎片卖给 Mechanic。即使在他人看来的“玩具”，落在他手里可能会再次变得危险。
69001c6cc637c00f150e3648.textEn: I decided not to sell the fragment to Mechanic. A "toy" like that in his hands could turn dangerous again.

69001c78384a9902240dee5c.textCh:
经历了这么长时间之后，Mechanic 不认为我们还能追查到 #1156 项目的进一步信息了。

看来我得自己想办法查明真相。1156 项目很有可能就是在本地的 TerraGroup 设施中进行的，甚至是就地组装起来的。
69001c78384a9902240dee5c.textEn:
Mechanic doesn’t believe it’s possible to get any more information on Item 1156 after all this time.

Looks like I’ll have to figure it out on my own. The work on Project 1156 might have been carried out at the local TerraGroup facilities.

69001c84e85e475e590c752b.textCh: 在实验室里我找到了一张字条，指示某人把 #1156 项目的蓝图以邮件的方式寄出去。市区里就有一家俄罗斯邮政的分局，说不定就是在那里寄出的——也许我可以从那里追踪这个包裹？
